On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.
summary_zh: 机器人使用智能体（RUAs）已成为通用机器人控制的一种重要方法。然而，目前只有GPT-6 Astra和Claude Fable 5.2等前沿专有模型能够实现强劲性能，而开源权重模型的能力仍明显不足。我们证明，一个270亿参数的开源推理模型可以通过强化学习，在完全模拟环境中且无需演示数据的情况下，被训练为原生使用真实机器人。与计算机使用智能体（CUA）类似，该模型观察环境、以思维链方式进行推理，并生成下一个末端执行器位姿，无需任何外部辅助框架。我们构建了一个面向智能体机器人的后训练引擎（PEAR），并利用该引擎通过机器人使用强化学习（RURL）在模拟机器人任务上进行大规模训练，这镜像了前沿模型获得计算机使用能力的方式。我们发现，在模拟中获得的技能能够很好地泛化到训练任务之外：它们可以迁移到未见过的新型机器人、真实世界以及新颖指令。在模拟环境中基于LIBERO和RoboDojo训练后，该模型在真实双臂机器人上的试验成功率达到60%，而基础模型的成功率为零。在LIBERO上，训练将成功率从1.6%提升至74.4%，在最大推理努力下接近GPT-6 Astra和GPT-6.1 Sol的水平。与基于演示数据微调得到的视觉-语言-动作模型π_{0.5}相比，我们的模型在面对任务本身的变化时具有更强的鲁棒性。在LIBERO-Pro上，π_{0.5}在熟悉场景中被分配新任务时仅在0.75%的回合中成功，而我们的模型成功率达到57.4%。最后，该模型保持了其通用能力，在九项推理、编码和视觉基准测试上没有出现可测量的性能退化。这些结果突显了机器人使用强化学习作为基础模型后训练中一个颇具前景的组成部分。
tldr: This paper introduces PEAR, a post-training engine that uses robot-use reinforcement learning entirely in simulation to train an open-weight 27B reasoning model to natively control real robots, achieving high success rates on real dual-arm robots and novel tasks without demonstrations.
tldr_zh: 本文介绍了PEAR，一种完全在仿真中通过机器人使用强化学习训练开源的27B推理模型，使其原生控制真实机器人，在真实双臂机器人和新任务上取得高成功率，且无需演示。

title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners
summary: Cooperative self-play can teach a humanoid to receive an object without any human data, but the partner it meets after training is never the one it trained with; we show that a fluent self-play handover policy breaks with unfamiliar partners, identify the main cause, and repair it. In a physics-based parcel handover between a Unitree G1 and a learned giver, both trained by alternating PPO self-play, the receiver completes 95% and 90% of handovers with its own partner (two training seeds) but only 31% with scripted partners it has never met. Paired interventions isolate the cause: under a shared reward the learned giver always starts its offer at once, so the receiver learns a single rendezvous, and delaying its own partner by one second cuts success from 95% to 6% (87% to 34% in the second seed). We introduce hidden start-delay randomisation (HSD), a one-line rule on the learned partner that the receiver never observes. After 300 further updates, success with unseen scripted partners rises from 31% to 80% in both seeds, against 35--41% for a budget-matched control. The gain holds on a fresh scenario seed, on eleven held-out partner conditions and on partners that start later than any training delay; it cuts high-force contact three- to five-fold and needs no retraining of the partner.
summary_zh: 合作式自我对弈可以在无需任何人类数据的情况下，教会一个人形机器人接收物体，但训练完成后它所遇到的伙伴并非训练时的伙伴；我们发现，流畅的自我对弈传递策略在面对陌生伙伴时会失效，我们找出了主要原因并对其进行了修复。在Unitree G1与一个学习型给予者之间基于物理引擎的包裹传递任务中，双方均通过交替PPO自我对弈进行训练，接收者与其自身伙伴（两个训练种子）完成传递的成功率分别为95%和90%，而与从未见过的脚本化伙伴合作时成功率仅为31%。配对干预实验隔离了原因：在共享奖励机制下，学习型给予者总是立即开始提供物体，因此接收者只学会了一种固定的会合方式；将自身伙伴的行为延迟一秒后，成功率从95%降至6%（第二个种子中从87%降至34%）。我们引入了隐藏起始延迟随机化（HSD）方法，这是对学习型伙伴的一条简单规则修改，接收者对此完全不可见。经过额外300次更新后，在两个种子中，接收者与未见过的脚本化伙伴的合作成功率从31%提升至80%，而预算匹配的对照组仅为35%至41%。该提升在新的场景种子、十一种保留的伙伴条件以及比任何训练延迟都更晚开始行动的伙伴身上均保持稳定；同时，高力度接触减少了三至五倍，且无需对伙伴进行重新训练。
tldr: The paper identifies that self-play handover policies for humanoid robots break with unfamiliar partners due to learned partners always starting offers immediately, and introduces hidden start-delay randomization (HSD) to make the receiver robust to unseen partners, improving success from 31% to 80% without retraining the partner.
tldr_zh: 本文发现自博弈交接策略在面对不熟悉伙伴时会失效，原因是学习到的给予者总是立即开始递出物品；通过引入隐藏起始延迟随机化（HSD），使接收者对未见过的伙伴更加鲁棒，成功率从31%提升到80%。

title: Disturbance-Aware Informative Planning in Spatiotemporal Environments
summary: Autonomous robots are widely used for persistent monitoring of spatiotemporal environments, where quantities of interest (QoI) change across space and time and require repeated measurements. In practice, robot motion can be affected by external disturbances that vary across the environment. When such external disturbances are not considered in trajectory optimization, it can lead to inaccurate predictions of robot motion and, consequently, the information acquired about the QoI during execution. However, estimating disturbances throughout the environment can be inefficient, as disturbances in regions with little overlap with monitoring trajectories have limited impact on monitoring performance. We therefore propose a two-stage informative planning framework for unknown, spatially varying but time-invariant disturbances, combining informed disturbance sampling with disturbance-aware trajectory optimization. First, we identify where QoI measurements are needed and generate alternative paths to these locations using the environment geometry. We then prioritize disturbance measurements based on their expected reduction of disturbance uncertainty along these paths. Second, rather than optimizing information acquisition based on nominal robot motion, we incorporate the learned disturbance belief into trajectory optimization to account for its effects on robot motion and information acquisition. Across four simulation scenarios, the proposed method reduces disturbance-learning time by 25.0--52.3 percent compared with environment-wide estimation and identifies paths that appear costly under nominal dynamics but become preferable when disturbances are considered.
summary_zh: 自主机器人被广泛应用于时空环境的持续监测，其中关注量随空间和时间变化，需要重复测量。在实践中，机器人运动可能受到随环境变化的外部扰动影响。若在轨迹优化中未考虑此类外部扰动，可能导致对机器人运动的预测不准确，进而影响执行过程中获取的关注量信息。然而，对整个环境中的扰动进行估计可能效率低下，因为与监测轨迹重叠较少的区域中的扰动对监测性能的影响有限。为此，我们提出了一种针对未知、空间变化但时间不变的扰动的两阶段信息规划框架，将知情扰动采样与扰动感知轨迹优化相结合。首先，我们确定需要关注量测量的位置，并利用环境几何生成到达这些位置的替代路径。随后，我们根据扰动测量沿这些路径对扰动不确定性的预期减少量，对其优先级进行排序。其次，我们不基于名义机器人运动优化信息采集，而是将学习到的扰动信念融入轨迹优化中，以考虑其对机器人运动和信息采集的影响。在四个仿真场景中，与全环境估计方法相比，所提方法将扰动学习时间减少了25.0%至52.3%，并识别出在名义动力学下看似成本较高、但在考虑扰动后更优的路径。
tldr: This paper proposes a two-stage informative planning framework that learns spatially varying disturbances along monitoring trajectories and incorporates them into trajectory optimization to improve information acquisition in spatiotemporal environments.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种两阶段信息规划框架，沿监测轨迹学习空间变化的扰动，并将其纳入轨迹优化，以提高时空环境中的信息采集效率。

title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
summary: Accurate friction modeling in continuum robots is essential for precise motion control and path planning. However, current approaches make predictions only for the mechanism's internal friction that is limited by the boundary forces of the Coulomb friction cone, which fail to characterize the static friction and motion hysteresis. In this paper, we propose a novel friction model based on complementarity constraints under the Coulomb friction assumption. This model predicts various friction effects caused by environmental interactions, including both static and sliding frictions and hysteresis behavior, as well as the corresponding robot deformation induced by these interactions, which are crucial for the practical motion planning and control of continuum robots. Additionally, real-time implementation of this model can be achieved, meeting the demand for computational efficiency in robotic applications. Experimental validations demonstrated that this model is able to reduce the maximum tip position error from 45.4 mm in the frictionless model to 5.85 mm in our friction-included model with a 287.9 mm-long tendon-driven continuum robot.
tldr: This paper introduces a complementarity-based friction model for continuum robots that captures static/sliding friction and hysteresis during environmental contact, improving tip position accuracy from 45.4mm to 5.85mm in a tendon-driven robot.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出一种基于互补约束的连续体机器人摩擦模型，可预测静态/滑动摩擦和迟滞效应，并将尖端位置误差从45.4mm降至5.85mm。

title: In Situ Monitoring and Predictive Modeling of Harmful Algal Blooms with Autonomous Surface Vehicles
summary: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) pose significant environmental, economic, and public-health challenges in coastal and inland water bodies, creating a need for scalable methods to collect spatially distributed water-quality data. This paper presents an autonomous surface vessel-based sensing system for in-situ water-quality monitoring related to harmful algal bloom detection. The system integrates a BlueBoat Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV), a motorized winch for depth-controlled sonde deployment, a multiparameter water-quality sonde, side-scan sonar, and an event-camera payload. Autonomous waypoint missions were used to collect measurements across selected sampling regions and multiple depths, enabling both horizontal and vertical characterization of environmental conditions. Field deployments were conducted in Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana, with additional measurements collected in False River, Louisiana to increase dataset diversity. The collected measurements included algal pigment indicators, nutrient concentration, turbidity, temperature, and other water-quality parameters relevant to bloom formation. In addition, complementary sonar and event-camera data were collected during vehicle operation to provide contextual environmental information. A machine-learning classification approach was also evaluated using the collected water-quality measurements to support HAB and non-HAB classification. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using a modular ASV platform for repeatable, multi-modal water-quality data collection and support future development of autonomous monitoring systems.
tldr: This paper presents and evaluates an autonomous surface vessel (ASV) system for in-situ water-quality monitoring and harmful algal bloom detection, integrating multiple sensors and a machine-learning classifier for HAB classification.
tldr_zh: 本文介绍并评估了一种用于原位水质监测和有害藻华检测的自主水面航行器（ASV）系统，集成了多种传感器和一种机器学习分类器，用于HAB分类。

title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions
summary: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific research by integrating robotics, automated experimentation, and machine learning to execute experiments autonomously. Biology and chemistry have adopted these systems. However, increasing SDL complexity heightens susceptibility to unexpected faults in automated workflows, highlighting the need for efficient recovery mechanisms. In this study, we investigate telerobotic interventions to enhance SDL resilience against unexpected failures. We developed a teleoperation interface enabling human operators to resolve disruptions during automated tasks. The interface enables precise control of a six-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robotic arm (UR3e) using a 3D mouse (3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Pro). Two velocity-based controller strategies were evaluated: (i) a coupled mode mapping all six DOFs to the 3D mouse's central knob and (ii) a decoupled mode separating translational and rotational motions. To evaluate the framework, teleoperators intervened across three SDL fault scenarios. In the first study, comparative trials showed that the decoupled controller was associated with shorter completion times and reduced rotational motion. In a second study, teleoperators performed an aiming task with and without reference-path guidance. Users were more target-driven and risk-tolerant without guidance but showed behavioral differences under different guidance strategies. These findings suggest that controller configuration and reference-path design influence operator performance during SDL fault recovery, informing teleoperation interface optimization. This work demonstrates the potential feasibility of teleoperation as a human-in-the-loop recovery mechanism for SDL workflows, combining robotic precision with human adaptability and problem-solving. These findings also provide a foundation for future studies in shared autonomy and semi-autonomous intervention.
tldr: This paper investigates telerobotic interventions for fault recovery in self-driving laboratories, evaluating two control strategies and guidance methods for a UR3e robotic arm to improve operator performance and system resilience.
tldr_zh: 本文研究了远程机器人干预在自动驾驶实验室故障恢复中的应用，评估了UR3e机械臂的两种控制策略和引导方法，以提高操作员性能和系统韧性。

title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible for a single person to teleoperate multiple agents simultaneously. Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) addresses this by letting a single demonstrator control one agent at a time while the others execute their current policies. However, the resulting imitation policies are limited by the quality of the demonstrations. We propose Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL), a framework that extends Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning (IBRL) to cooperative teams and uses R2BC to train the imitation policies. At each time step, every agent receives one action proposal from its imitation policy and one from its RL policy, and an ensemble of centralized critics selects among the per-agent combinations of the two. A gated imitation penalty, a soft Q-filtered behavior cloning loss, regularizes each RL policy toward its imitation policy only where the critics value the imitation action more, so that after training each agent executes its RL policy alone, without the centralized critics. On four cooperative multi-agent RL benchmarks, IBMARL surpasses its imitation policies $2.6$-$4.2\times$ faster than demonstration-based baselines on two tasks, is the only method to surpass it on the other two, and exceeds the demonstrator itself on two of the four. With real human demonstrations IBMARL still surpasses imitation learning alone, and does so more than twice as fast as the best baseline.
tldr: IBMARL extends imitation bootstrapped RL to cooperative multi-agent settings, using round-robin behavior cloning to train imitation policies and an ensemble of centralized critics to combine imitation and RL proposals, improving sample efficiency and surpassing demonstrator performance on benchmarks and with human demonstrations.
tldr_zh: IBMARL将模仿引导强化学习扩展到多智能体协作场景，通过循环行为克隆和集中式评论家集成来结合模仿与RL动作，显著提升样本效率并在多个基准上超越演示者表现。

title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
summary: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification. We introduce \textbf{ARCHER}: \textbf{A}ction-trace \textbf{R}einforcement for \textbf{C}alculator-grounded \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{R}easoning, a two-stage framework for training small language models (SLMs) to produce executable and auditable reasoning trajectories. In the first stage, ARCHER compiles free-form chain-of-thought rationales into typed action traces containing reasoning steps, calculator calls, deterministic runtime observations, verification actions, and final answers. This shifts the supervision target from imitating explanatory text to learning a tool-grounded reasoning policy. In the second stage, ARCHER refines this policy through asymmetric hierarchical reinforcement learning, using grouped and conditionally gated trajectory rewards for answer correctness, tool grounding, process discipline, and trace alignment. Across five standard sub-10B backbones, ARCHER improves over the strongest tool-augmented baseline by 5.51 percentage points on macro-average across benchmark accuracies, including gains of 8.95 points on MATH-500 and 5.33 and 5.34 points on AIME-2024 and AIME-2025. Evaluations on two additional reasoning-specialized 7B backbones further show that executable grounding remains beneficial after reasoning-focused reinforcement learning or distillation. These results demonstrate that executable supervision and reward-guided behavioral refinement provide a general and effective training paradigm for compact mathematical reasoners.

title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
summary: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. The full stack of quantum computing encompasses several tasks: preparation of logical code states, implementation of logical gates, logical routines on encoded qubits, etc. Yet, these circuits are largely designed by hand for individual cases, with some recent works incorporating machine learning for certain aspects. We formulate this problem as agentic evolutionary program synthesis, wherein a large language model, leveraging its pretraining knowledge and tool-use proficiency, and guided by a circuit verifier, evolves a program that defines a Clifford circuit for a wide range of curated tasks such as logical state preparation, logical gate design, and logical routines such as code-switching, code growth, etc. Our approach consistently finds fault-tolerant circuits for all of these tasks, each verified by an exhaustive check over faults.

title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise, even where humans never reward it. A learned policy instead converges to the tradeoffs rewarded by its environment; when humans supply the rewards, we call this socialization. Accumulated experience makes socialization harder to reverse under subsequent task-only training, although violations can arise before the prevailing disposition changes, and finite memory weakens this protection. When a single violation can end a deployment, a hard prohibition can prevent it, but a mistaken prohibition can also be costly. Experiments with small neural networks illustrate how training targets and memory shape these outcomes. Our results suggest that alignment depends not only on the objectives assigned to agents, but also on the environments that shape and sustain their behavior.

title: Asymptotic Margins and Feature Confinement in Conic Classification Heads under Softmax Cross-Entropy
summary: Classification heads built on conic functions give each class a bounded region of the feature space, and such regions are used to reject samples of unseen classes. We ask whether these regions also keep the features bounded when the head is trained with softmax cross-entropy. For a head whose class scores combine a linear term with a Euclidean norm, we first show that the region of each class is bounded by a quadric of revolution, whose eccentricity is the reciprocal of one learned ratio. We then attach to each class an asymptotic margin, which compares the growth of its score with the growth of all the other scores and can be computed by a second-order cone program. The loss of a class has infimum zero exactly when its margin is positive, and it then approaches zero only along diverging features. When the margin is negative, the loss is coercive and its minimizers lie in an explicit ball. Since softmax depends only on the differences between scores, a class with a bounded region can still have a positive margin, so bounded regions do not confine the features. The result extends to other norms, including the polyhedral conic functions. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, all 1210 cells of 67 trained conic heads have positive margins, whereas a prototype head keeps nine of its ten cells bounded, as the theory predicts.

title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
summary: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.

title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
summary: Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) objects is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of object detectors in real-world deployment. We treat the decision on a detected box as a hypothesis test with the null hypothesis that the box covers an object of an in-distribution (ID) class. The null distribution changes with the size of the box and its contact with the image border, and the detector observes both. The test can therefore rank a box only against ID boxes of the same size and border contact, which gives a distribution-free bound on the false-alarm rate for each of them and uncovers the separation that one null distribution hides. The power of the test also rests on the layer it reads. Layers built only for the ID classes have no reason to keep what sets an unknown object apart, so the test reads the features before them. We propose \textbf{PLUM}, a training-free score that pools the last backbone stage inside the box and ranks its distance to the ID classes among ID boxes of the same size and border contact. On the standard benchmark, PLUM reaches the highest AUROC among the compared methods without external models, with 91.5 and 94.5 on PASCAL-VOC and 95.1 and 97.5 on BDD100K. Code: https://github.com/DDOZMI/PLUM

title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions. However, these results only provide a partial explanation of why the agent hallucinates. The probe direction is sensitive to prompt formatting, losing much of its steering effect after a minor change to how actions are represented. Additionally, circuit identification can be difficult as the computation is distributed across multiple components and positions, and the information the agent relies on varies across examples. We discuss how these observations challenge the assumptions underlying standard MI methods for circuit discovery and feature identification, and outline future directions for making these methods better suited to explain failures in LLM-based agents.

title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
summary: Generative modeling based on stochastic interpolants requires specifying two key choices: an interpolant schedule bridging the initial and target distributions, and an efficient discretization of the resulting probability-flow ODE. In this work, we introduce a new framework for joint schedule/discretization design based on the analyticity properties of the (complexified) ODE trajectories, which in turn ensure good numerical behavior. Our formulation can be solved exactly via conformal mapping, yielding a natural family of variance-preserving elliptic schedules, parametrized by Jacobi elliptic functions. Pairing an elliptic schedule with a tailored discretization, we obtain Zoloflow, a new sampling algorithm closely connected to Zolotarev's optimal rational function approximants. Crucially, both the elliptic schedule and Zoloflow explicitly incorporate the condition number $κ$ of the target distribution and reduce to the classical trig schedule in the limit $κ\rightarrow 1$. For Gaussian targets, Zoloflow achieves minimax optimality among all oblivious score-span algorithms, attaining total-variation error $\varepsilon$ using $Θ(\logκ\,\log(\sqrt d/\varepsilon))$ (exact) score queries. For the log-concave case, the elliptic schedule allows sampling with at most $\varepsilon$ 2-Wasserstein-error by requiring merely $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d} \, \mathrm{polylog}(κ, 1/\varepsilon))$ score evaluations. Complementing these theoretical results, we empirically evaluate the elliptic schedule on general (non-log-concave) target distributions, including detailed comparisons with alternative schedule proposals on both synthetic benchmarks and existing image generation datasets.

title: EventSpikeSeg: Memory-Aware Mixed-Signal Architecture for Event-Camera Spiking Segmentation
summary: Event-camera segmentation requires persistent neural state despite sparse input events, making memory organization a central constraint on embedded implementation. We present EventSpikeSeg, a mixed-signal architecture combining resident capacitor memory with shared analog processing in GF180MCU 180-nm CMOS. Its 25-population spiking encoder-decoder has 143,824 synaptic weights but requires 30,976,000 membrane states at 440 x 640 resolution. The mapping specifies chronological 5-ms model updates, digital event/address services and 64-state capacitor banks. Characterization covers 22 module families and 74 operating points, distinguishing transistor simulations from digital-library estimates. Nominal results include 41.711 microwatts biased neuron-core power, 3.338-pJ positive terminal energy for a 1.4-microsecond cell read, and 0.531-mV selected-state drift over a 5-ms extracted-tile hold. Commit and coupling errors are reported separately. The software checkpoint records 27.976% mean intersection-over-union on a held-out six-class DSEC split; this is not hardware accuracy. Component layouts and simulation evidence quantify local implementation costs and expose storage replication and service scheduling as scaling constraints. A detailed SPICE-calibrated behavioral forward simulation of one full-resolution DSEC frame achieves 24.26% mean intersection-over-union, versus 26.22% for the matched PyTorch reference, using a compact 5-fF bank variant and external count/voltage calibration. Physical full-network operation, system energy and mismatch robustness remain unverified.

title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
summary: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices. When evaluated using publicly available data from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis user, FETTUCCINE outperforms previous end-to-end methods, achieving as low as 4.39% WER. Most notably, our models successfully run on a commercially-available mobile device with throughput reaching up to 370x real-time, providing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on a mobile device. We also show that our models can be successfully finetuned to extend usable performance to future days. Beyond performance, our approach enables localization of the neural features most relevant for decoding via gradient-based saliency maps, which we show align with well-established physiological priors across different ASR model families. Taken together, our results show that FETTUCCINE overcomes core infrastructural and computational barriers, yielding a new class of portable brain-to-text communication.

title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
summary: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.

title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
summary: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. The system integrates a hybrid retrieval architecture, combining vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings, to ensure high fidelity to the reader's current context. We evaluate the system across classical English books using both quantitative comprehension metrics and qualitative LLM-based independent judging. The results identify a quality-latency frontier, showing that mid-sized local models (2b-4b) can achieve comprehension parity with larger counterparts (5b+) while maintaining acceptable response quality. Importantly, the proposed progress-aware boundary mechanism is shown to prevent future content leakage without compromising retrieval quality and correctness. These findings suggest that a localized, privacy-centric approach can augment, rather than replace, the digital reading experience, offering a good alternative to cloud-dependent services. Therein, there remains a lack of amalgamate systems which combine progress-aware, privacy-preserving, and narrative eBook reading with AI support. It is in this very gap that the development of MeReader came to be; synthesizing said strands into an offline, book-constrained assistant focused on enhancing comprehension without compromising narrative continuity or user privacy.

title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. Most existing approaches train under a hand-written harness that stays fixed throughout. However, an effective harness depends on the domain, the data and the model, and keeps changing as the model trains. We introduce ModHarness-RL, which recasts the harness as programs that are learned from data and evolve as the model trains with RL. ModHarness-RL records the interaction as structured State, a set of typed blocks, and two core components of the harness are programs over these blocks, a Compression program that assembles the accumulated history into the model's context and a Steering program that supplies guidance when behavior deviates. During RL training, candidate programs are proposed from recent trajectories, verified by execution, and replayed over past trajectories, so the harness tracks how the model's behavior shifts. We study CodeSearch in depth and further analyze ALFWorld and BIRD SQL, with models from 1.5B to 8B. The proposed Compression and Steering mechanisms improve held-out performance over the fixed-harness baseline in most settings. These results suggest that a harness for agentic RL can be learned from the task's data and evolved with the model.

title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
summary: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.

title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
summary: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. In contrast, space-based radio frequency (RF) observations provide an independent source of vessel activity but lack ship identification and therefore cannot identify vessels on their own. Following the CRISP-DM process, this study applies a Pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM) to align individual RF detections with AIS trajectories, using temporal and spatial information while modeling noise and timing discrepancies. We evaluate it on NOAA AIS data with synthetic RF detections against nearest-neighbor baselines and analyze its errors with bias tests on trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity and AIS--RF distance. The length-corrected Forward score reaches a top-1 precision of $0.7776$ on the validation split of multi-candidate detections, where errors are possible, and an AUC of $0.637$ for detecting dark vessels among the detections that pass the prefilter. With a single RF detection, the score mostly reflects the AIS trajectory itself, and its errors favor longer and more stationary trajectories. A log-odds score, which compares the full model with a null model without match transitions, raises precision to $0.8580$ and AUC to $0.852$. Its length-corrected variant no longer shows a significant bias towards stationary trajectories and short inter-message distances, but still favors candidates farther from the RF detection. A time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without fitting remains ahead (precision $0.9013$, AUC $0.904$), so this single-detection, hand-designed PHMM formulation approaches but does not beat it.

title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
summary: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmarks, ReDiverse consistently restores sample diversity while preserving generation quality, further supported by the user study.

title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
summary: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots. This raises a question: do visual encoders need to recompute their representations from scratch for every new screenshot? We present StreamEmbed, a system for incremental visual embedding that exploits this redundancy. Guided solely by pixel differences, it combines spatial token pruning, which skips blocks that repeat a neighbor, with temporal KV reuse, which reuses cached keys and values for blocks unchanged across screenshots. A small learned adapter compensates for pruning and reuse to preserve fidelity to full-screenshot embeddings. On ScreenMemEval, our benchmark of 10,426 questions over 184 hours of screen histories from two humans and a computer-use agent, StreamEmbed sets a new accuracy-latency Pareto frontier on an M2 Pro GPU: it encodes up to 3.7x faster than full-screenshot encoding without sacrificing accuracy and improves accuracy over OCR-based indexing by up to 6.3 Recall@10 points at matched latency. A memory-efficient vector index stores a simulated year of screenshots in 0.13 GB of RAM. Together, these results make real-time indexing of screen history in its native visual form practical, laying a foundation for fully local visual assistants.

title: TradeGauntlet: Evaluating Compliance Controls for Autonomous Trading Agents
summary: Autonomous trading agents need controls that prevent problematic orders without making legitimate tasks impractical. We study this aspect of agentic compliance with TradeGauntlet, a replayable limit-order-book simulator that separates detection, prevention, and execution cost. In 1,680 simulated sessions with Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, all conduct alerts were self-matches. Gates eliminated those alerts by rejecting self-crossing orders, while the aggregate-gate condition reduced Sonnet's two-sided fills by about 15%. A conduct reminder reduced Sonnet's alert rate but reduced Haiku's fills without a detectable alert benefit. These results show why zero alerts alone do not establish an agent's compliance. Scripted probes and two search methods test weaknesses beyond those observed in the LLM runs. The searches find split-order schedules that evade the implemented conduct rules; a learned baseline catches all 2,400 tested searched episodes but also flags 15% of a large maker's sessions. Aggregate caps reduce the response-dependent gain unevenly, with smaller reductions when only near-touch depth affects prices. A response fitted to five Nasdaq stocks and a separate ABIDES experiment expose the dependence of these estimates on market assumptions. A distinct adversarial prompt elicited refusals from Sonnet in all 240 rounds, yielding no candidate strategies to evaluate. TradeGauntlet provides reproducible tests of controls around trading agents; the experiments do not establish legal compliance or real-market detection accuracy.

title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
summary: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) can classify images using background-dominated patches that contain little or none of the target object, showing that they exploit contextual information. Previous studies detected this behavior through classification accuracy but say little about what CNN hidden layers represent. We investigate whether Concept Induction can reveal interpretable visual properties associated with hidden-neuron activations on contextual image patches. Using five agricultural datasets with high, moderate, and low contextual bias, we analyze four CNN architectures at three network depths and five patch locations. Quantitative image descriptors of each patch are encoded in a knowledge graph and used as background knowledge for Concept Induction, which derives logical expressions characterizing neuron activation. These expressions are tested on held-out images using the Mann-Whitney U test and Cliff's delta. Of 48,013 tested neuron-feature pairs, 13,164 (27.4%) were validated. Validation was most frequent at intermediate depths (mean 40.2% at mid layers versus 12.0% at deep layers), and no patch location dominated across datasets. Among the tested descriptors, edge, Gabor, and Tamura texture features had the highest validation rates. Stronger contextual bias did not correspond to higher neuron-feature validation rates: moderately biased Sugarcane had the highest rate (40.5%) and highly biased Cassava the lowest (19.2%). These results suggest that behavioral context dependence and the semantic interpretability of hidden neurons capture different aspects of CNN behavior, and that Concept Induction can complement patch-based bias detection.

title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
summary: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. On all 42 tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215); on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546. Code, the task registry, our OS-level sandbox harness, and the live leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench.

title: Why Finite Intelligence Works in an Infinite World: A Mathematical Theory
summary: An information system often has to learn before it knows what it will be asked. A finite representation can succeed without recording an infinite environment in full when those asks share collective structure, rather than demand unrelated facts scattered arbitrarily across it. We formalize this phenomenon through future-task information, the minimum retained information needed to preserve decision value relative to the available evidence. A joint decision-regret state records posterior comparisons among actions for every permitted task. Under compactness assumptions, every retained representation admits a calibrated replacement based on this state, preserving all task regrets without increasing information; the resulting information-regret curve equals an operational coding rate. Two exact boundaries govern finite preservation: weak-star closure for a fixed action count, and the singular mass of the source-evidence law when all finite action menus are admitted. Collective structure determines information requirements beyond individual-question difficulty. Families with identical source laws, pairwise task metrics, and individual-task rates can have different high-resolution exponents. Covariance-identical coordinate and parity families have different exact rate-distortion curves, with optimal parity retention characterized by a sharp Fourier-entropy inequality. For balanced nested task families, refinement sizes and weighted reach determine the rate within an additive constant, attained by prefix coding under explicit decay conditions. Nonlinear learning and computational separations distinguish preservation from efficient discovery and use. The proposed mathematical theory identifies which shared decision requirements allow finite information to remain useful for infinitely many possible purposes.

title: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
summary: World-action models (WAMs) augment vision-language-action policies (VLAs) with future prediction so that the policy can anticipate how its actions will affect the physical world. Existing WAMs supervise complete future observations. However, observations typically change little over an action chunk, so the future loss is dominated by copying static background content rather than learning task-relevant robot and object motion, limiting policy learning. Moreover, existing WAMs rely on large video generation models or separate world models, incurring heavy training and inference compute that hinders closed-loop deployment. To improve policy performance, we propose visual residual learning, supervising only the feature change from the current frame to the future frame in a frozen DINOv3 space. Compared with complete future features, this residual learning target yields a higher feature rank with richer and more diverse representations of scene changes, and spatially concentrates on the robot arm and manipulated objects rather than the background. To further improve computational efficiency, we present ResWAM, a residual world-action model with 2.3B parameters in total, including a lightweight 0.5B dual-branch DiT that jointly trains an action branch and a residual branch via conditional flow matching. Without robot pretraining (i.e., pretraining on external robot action trajectories beyond the benchmark demonstrations), ResWAM achieves top average success rates on LIBERO-Plus (81.1%), RoboTwin 2.0 (93.8%), and RoboDojo (9.40% success, 13.41 score) at the lowest training (2.7-4.0 TFLOPs) and inference compute (1.0-1.4 TFLOPs), and leads real-robot Open, Put, and Stack (80.0% average, +10.0% over $π_{0.5}$) at 92.7 ms latency.
summary_zh: 世界动作模型（WAMs）通过未来预测增强视觉-语言-动作策略（VLAs），使策略能够预判其动作对物理世界的影响。现有WAMs对完整的未来观测进行监督，然而，在动作片段内观测通常变化甚微，因此未来损失主要被静态背景内容的复制所主导，而非学习与任务相关的机器人和物体运动，从而限制了策略学习。此外，现有WAMs依赖大规模视频生成模型或独立的 world models，导致训练和推理计算开销沉重，阻碍了闭环部署。为提升策略性能，我们提出视觉残差学习，在冻结的 DINOv3 空间中仅监督当前帧到未来帧的特征变化。与完整的未来特征相比，该残差学习目标产生更高的特征秩，蕴含更丰富、更多样化的场景变化表示，并在空间上集中于机械臂和被操作物体，而非背景。为进一步提升计算效率，我们提出 ResWAM，一个总参数量为 2.3B 的残差世界动作模型，其中包含一个轻量级 0.5B 双分支 DiT，通过条件流匹配联合训练动作分支和残差分支。在不进行机器人预训练（即不利用基准演示之外的机器人动作轨迹进行预训练）的情况下，ResWAM 在 LIBERO-Plus（81.1%）、RoboTwin 2.0（93.8%）和 RoboDojo（成功率 9.40%，得分 13.41）上以最低的训练（2.7-4.0 TFLOPs）和推理计算量（1.0-1.4 TFLOPs）取得最高平均成功率，并在真实机器人 Open、Put 和 Stack 任务中以 92.7 ms 延迟取得领先表现（平均 80.0%，较 π₀.₅ 提升 10.0%）。
tldr: ResWAM introduces visual residual learning for world-action models, predicting only feature changes rather than full future frames, which improves policy learning efficiency and performance on simulation and real-robot tasks.
tldr_zh: ResWAM 提出视觉残差学习方法，仅预测未来帧的特征变化而非完整帧，从而提高世界动作模型的策略学习效率和性能，在仿真和真实机器人任务中表现优异。

title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
summary: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one $360^\circ$ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched $360^\circ$ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at $8$-$46\times$ their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.
summary_zh: 驾驶世界模型通常从六个具有独立光学中心和较小重叠区域的针孔摄像头生成视频，并且必须学习保持这些视图的一致性。我们提出了PanDWM，它将这六个视图拼接成一个$360^\circ$全景带。摄像头边界随后落在一张图像内部，因此保持视图一致就意味着保持图像连续，同时每个像素仍然记录其对应的摄像头光线。在布局条件的约束下，一个因果学生模型以四步窗口方式逐窗口生成该全景带；它从因果教师模型中蒸馏得到，并在自身的展开轨迹上进行训练。一个前馈解码器将每一帧沿这些光线提升为3D高斯体，相邻帧的静态高斯体将它们补全为4D场景。在nuScenes数据集上，以拼接后的单一$360^\circ$视图进行评分，PanDWM的FID和FVD均低于多摄像头基线方法，同时速度是其$8$至$46$倍，并且在保持其50步教师模型FID的同时，将FVD降低了22-25%。
tldr: PanDWM stitches multi-camera driving video into a single 360-degree panoramic band, and trains a causal student world model distilled from a teacher to generate consistent 4D driving scenes more efficiently. It improves FVD over multi-camera baselines on nuScenes while being 8-46x faster.
tldr_zh: PanDWM将多相机驾驶视频拼接成360度全景带，并训练从教师模型蒸馏出的因果学生世界模型，以更高效地生成一致的4D驾驶场景。在nuScenes上相比多相机基线降低了FVD，同时速度提升8-46倍。

title: Cleanly-DINO: Efficiently Learning Visual Task Spaces for Robotics
summary: Learning manipulation tasks from few demonstrations requires abstractions that capture the changes relevant to task completion, such as object poses in rigid-body manipulation. However, tasks such as cleaning are defined by changes in visual state rather than object pose, making the choice of task representation less clear. In this work, we propose Cleanly-DINO to learn visual task spaces from few demonstrations. Given a mask of a task-relevant region and frozen ViT features, Cleanly-DINO fits a projection to isolate a task space and fit a progression metric to it. We train the model on diverse cleaning examples and evaluate its ability to localize incomplete task regions and transfer across visual domains. We also study its utility for robot learning by using it as an observation encoder and reward signal in a reinforcement learning setting. Finally, we deploy our fitted model within a real-world robotic wiping pipeline to evaluate its use in guiding task execution.
authors: José Arce y de la Borbolla
summary_zh: 从少量示范中学习操控任务，需要抽象出与任务完成相关的状态变化，例如刚体操控中的物体位姿。然而，诸如清洁等任务是由视觉状态的变化而非物体位姿来定义的，这使得任务表示的选择变得不那么明确。在本工作中，我们提出Cleanly-DINO，用于从少量示范中学习视觉任务空间。给定任务相关区域的掩码和冻结的ViT特征，Cleanly-DINO拟合一个投影以隔离任务空间，并对其拟合一个进度度量。我们在多样化的清洁示例上训练该模型，并评估其在定位未完成任务区域及跨视觉域迁移方面的能力。我们还通过将其用作强化学习设置中的观测编码器和奖励信号，研究其在机器人学习中的实用性。最后，我们在真实世界的机器人擦拭流程中部署所拟合的模型，以评估其在指导任务执行中的应用。
tldr: Cleanly-DINO learns visual task spaces from few demonstrations for cleaning tasks, fitting a projection onto frozen ViT features to isolate task-relevant progress, and is evaluated as a reward signal for RL and deployed in a real-world robotic wiping pipeline.
tldr_zh: Cleanly-DINO 从少量演示中学习清洁任务的视觉任务空间，通过将冻结的 ViT 特征投影到任务相关区域来拟合进度度量，并作为奖励信号用于强化学习及真实机器人擦拭任务。

title: SAFER: Navigating the Exploration-Exploitation Dilemma in World-Model-Based Planning for Autonomous Driving
summary: An autonomous vehicle must foresee the consequences of its actions, especially in the rare, time-critical situations where crashes happen. A world model offers this foresight, but only within the coverage of its training data, which poses an exploration-exploitation dilemma. Within this coverage a planner can hardly improve on the data, and beyond it the model's errors mislead it. Logs of competent driving rarely contain the failures that would widen the coverage, and agents that learn from interaction gain them only by failing themselves, without being shown what to do instead. We propose SAFER, a framework that learns offline from failures that others make, judged by an expert, and keeps learning online from its own driving. Offline, partially trained agents and scripted, recoverable perturbations Stage failures in simulation, and an expert Annotates every visited state with its action and value, so that much of what the planner explores is covered before it drives. In planning, a chunked latent world model Foresees the consequences fast enough for real-time use, and a risk-aware sampling-based planner Evaluates candidate maneuvers by their return minus a bounded collision penalty. Online, a loop continuously Refines the model wherever this driving leaves the coverage of the offline data. In closed-loop evaluation against the compared methods, SAFER reaches the highest route completion and reward per step on the CARLA Leaderboard routes, 0.95 and 0.77 from a privileged bird's-eye view, and the highest episode reward in MetaDrive, 53.4 in regular and 49.0 in safety-critical traffic. Project page: https://ys-qu.github.io/safer-website.
summary_zh: 自主驾驶车辆必须预见其行为带来的后果，尤其是在发生碰撞的罕见、时间紧迫的关键情境中。世界模型提供了这种预见能力，但其适用范围仅限于训练数据所覆盖的范围，这带来了探索与利用之间的两难困境。在该覆盖范围内，规划器难以在数据基础上有所改进；而超出覆盖范围，模型的误差又会误导规划器。称职驾驶的日志中很少包含能够扩大覆盖范围的失败案例，而通过交互学习的智能体只能通过自身犯错来获得这些失败经验，却未被展示应如何正确应对。我们提出SAFER框架，该框架离线学习他人所犯的、经专家评判的失败案例，并在线持续从自身驾驶中学习。离线阶段，部分训练的智能体和脚本化的可恢复扰动在仿真中构建失败场景，专家对每个访问到的状态标注其动作和价值，从而在规划器投入驾驶前，大部分探索范围已获覆盖。在规划阶段，分块潜世界模型快速预见后果以满足实时需求，基于风险感知的采样规划器通过“回报减去有界碰撞惩罚”来评估候选操作。在线阶段，一个闭环持续在驾驶偏离离线数据覆盖范围处精化模型。在与对比方法的闭环评估中，SAFER在CARLA Leaderboard路线上取得了最高的路线完成率和每步奖励，分别为0.95和0.77（基于特权鸟瞰视角），并在MetaDrive中取得了最高的回合奖励，常规交通下为53.4，安全关键交通下为49.0。项目页面：https://ys-qu.github.io/safer-website。
tldr: SAFER is a framework for world-model-based planning in autonomous driving that addresses the exploration-exploitation dilemma by learning offline from staged failures and annotating states with expert actions and values, then refining the model online. It uses a chunked latent world model and risk-aware sampling-based planner, achieving state-of-the-art route completion and reward in CARLA and MetaDrive benchmarks.
tldr_zh: SAFER 是一个用于自动驾驶中基于世界模型规划的新框架，通过离线从 staged failures 中学习并用专家行为和价值注释状态，再在线细化模型，来解决探索-利用困境。它使用分块潜在世界模型和风险感知的基于采样的规划器，在 CARLA 和 MetaDrive 基准测试中取得了最先进的路线完成率和奖励。

title: EgoSwarm: Learning Decentralized Robot Swarm Intelligence from Human Swarm Demonstrations
summary: Advancing from individual embodied intelligence to swarm embodied intelligence is a key step toward scalable, general-purpose embodied intelligence. Complex tasks often require multiple agents to divide responsibilities, coordinate handovers, and manipulate shared objects collaboratively. However, existing robot learning methods rely primarily on individual demonstrations, which provide limited supervision for modeling dependencies among agent actions, while collecting multi-robot demonstrations at scale remains difficult. Human egocentric demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, yet distributed observations from multiple participants cannot directly supervise decentralized policies. We introduce EgoSwarm, the first robot learning framework for learning decentralized multi-robot collaboration from human swarm demonstrations. EgoSwarm collects more than 50 hours of collaborative experience using a robot-free multi-person egocentric system. We introduce the Swarm Interaction Packet (SIP) and Swarm Interaction Token (SIT) to recover cross-agent interaction relations from distributed observations and transform this experience into local supervision consistent with deployment-time information constraints. We further propose SwarmVLA, which transfers knowledge of swarm behavior to decentralized policies conditioned on local observations, local history, and limited neighbor messages. SwarmVLA achieves a mean success rate of 72.2% across three categories of multi-robot collaborative tasks. Project page:https://xitong-c.github.io/EgoSwarm_Page/.
summary_zh: 从单体具身智能迈向群具身智能，是通向可扩展、通用具身智能的关键一步。复杂任务往往需要多个智能体分工协作、协调交接，并共同操作共享物体。然而，现有的机器人学习方法主要依赖单体示范，难以提供足够的监督信息来建模智能体间的动作依赖关系，而大规模采集多机器人示范数据又十分困难。人类自我中心视角的示范提供了一种可扩展的替代方案，但来自多个参与者的分布式观测无法直接监督去中心化策略。我们提出了EgoSwarm，这是首个从人类群体示范中学习去中心化多机器人协作的机器人学习框架。EgoSwarm利用无机器人多人在第一人称视角系统采集了超过50小时的协作经验。我们引入了群体交互数据包（SIP）和群体交互令牌（SIT），以从分布式观测中恢复跨智能体的交互关系，并将这些经验转化为与部署时信息约束一致的局部监督信号。我们进一步提出了SwarmVLA，将群体行为知识迁移到以局部观测、局部历史和有限邻居消息为条件的去中心化策略中。SwarmVLA在三类多机器人协作任务中实现了72.2%的平均成功率。项目页面：https://xitong-c.github.io/EgoSwarm_Page/。
tldr: EgoSwarm introduces a framework for learning decentralized multi-robot collaboration from human swarm demonstrations, using Swarm Interaction Packets (SIP) and Tokens (SIT) to recover cross-agent interactions and a SwarmVLA policy for local observation-conditioned control, achieving 72.2% success on collaborative tasks.
tldr_zh: EgoSwarm提出了一种从人类群体演示中学习去中心化多机器人协作的框架，利用群体交互包（SIP）和群体交互令牌（SIT）恢复跨智能体交互，并训练局部观测条件下的SwarmVLA策略，在协作任务中平均成功率72.2%。

title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged in autonomous driving with the promise of strong generalization to long-tail scenarios. Although these models achieve state-of-the-art results on autonomous driving benchmarks, most existing benchmarks are dominated by nominal scenarios and therefore cannot test this promise. To test one such long-tail capability that is critical for safety, we introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark that measures how driving models react to objects that appear in the ego vehicle's path. Built on real NAVSIM and PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles scenes, ReactBench-AD composites a crossing pedestrian, a standing pedestrian, or a stationary car consistently across all camera views and history frames. Each edited scene thus forms an exact, pixel-level counterfactual pair with its original, which allows us to isolate the causal effect of the inserted object on the predicted trajectory. Evaluating four VLAs and two WAMs, we find that they react weakly, often barely at all. Finally, we test how easily one of the evaluated VLAs, ReCogDrive, can be taught to brake hard for imminent hazards: a short fine-tuning stage on edited scenes substantially improves its reactions, with the learned behavior generalizing to unseen objects and fully real scenes, at minimal cost to nominal driving. These results call into question the out-of-the-box long-tail capabilities of these models, but suggest that they can be a strong foundation for acquiring them with little additional training, highlighting the value of real or synthetic data that demonstrates the long-tail behaviors nominal datasets rarely contain. Code and data will be made publicly available.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作模型（VLAs）和世界-动作模型（WAMs）已应用于自动驾驶领域，其优势在于对长尾场景具有强大的泛化能力。尽管这些模型在自动驾驶基准测试中取得了最先进的成绩，但现有的大多数基准测试以常规场景为主，无法真正检验这一能力。为了测试一项对安全至关重要的长尾能力，我们引入了ReactBench-AD，这是一个衡量驾驶模型对自车路径上出现的物体作出反应能力的基准。基于真实的NAVSIM和PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles场景，ReactBench-AD在所有相机视角和历史帧中一致地合成一个穿越的行人、一个站立的行人或一辆静止的车辆。因此，每个编辑后的场景与其原始场景构成一个精确的、像素级的反事实配对，使我们能够隔离插入物体对预测轨迹的因果影响。对四个VLA和两个WAM的评估结果显示，它们的反应普遍较弱，甚至几乎没有任何反应。最后，我们测试了所评估的VLA之一ReCogDrive，能否通过简单的训练学会对即将发生的危险进行紧急制动：在编辑场景上进行短暂微调后，该模型的反应显著改善，并且学习到的行为能够泛化到未见过的物体和完全真实的场景中，同时对常规驾驶的影响微乎其微。这些结果对这类模型开箱即用的长尾能力提出了质疑，但也表明它们可以作为以很少额外训练获得长尾能力的强大基础，凸显了展示长尾行为（常规数据集很少包含此类行为）的真实或合成数据的价值。代码和数据将公开发布。
tldr: ReactBench-AD is a benchmark that inserts counterfactual imminent hazards into real driving scenes to test whether driving VLAs and World-Action Models react by braking, finding weak reactions but showing that short fine-tuning can substantially improve hazard response.
tldr_zh: ReactBench-AD 通过在真实驾驶场景中插入反事实的迫近危险来测试驾驶 VLA 和世界动作模型是否会刹车，发现模型反应薄弱，但短暂微调可显著提升其对危险的反应能力。

title: PlanDiv: Test-Time Scaling with Latent Plans for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Test-time scaling improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies by drawing several action candidates and executing the best one. We find that its returns diminish quickly when the candidates are resampled from one decoder: they differ by noise rather than by plan, and for each of three resampling sources, going from four to eight candidates adds only 0.06-0.07 to the average number of completed tasks on CALVIN. We introduce PlanDiv, an action head that makes the candidates differ by plan: a lightweight planner proposes K latent plan hypotheses, a shared masked-diffusion executor decodes one action chunk per plan from a single backbone pass, and the policy executes the chunk that its own likelihood ranks highest. The plans are learned from demonstrations alone, without plan labels or rewards. With the backbone, data and training recipe held fixed, eight plan-conditioned candidates raise five-task chain success on CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D from 56.9% to 69.9%, while eight candidates from autoregressive, plan-free or same-plan resampling reach at most 64.9%. The same-plan baseline is PlanDiv's own checkpoint with the plan held fixed, so this gap comes from the plans, not from drawing more samples. On LIBERO-Long, four plans remove 40% of single-candidate failures, against at most 21% for matched resampling. On a real Franka arm the gain appears where a task admits more than one solution: PlanDiv is on par with a single-output OpenVLA-OFT+ baseline on a one-solution task and succeeds in 51 of 54 trials against 40 of 54 on two tasks with two solutions.
summary_zh: 测试时扩展通过抽取多个动作候选并执行最优者来提升视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略的性能。我们发现，当候选动作从同一解码器中重新采样时，其收益会迅速衰减：候选之间的差异来自噪声而非规划，并且在三种重采样来源中，从四个候选增加到八个候选，在CALVIN上平均完成的任务数仅增加0.06-0.07。我们提出PlanDiv，一种使候选动作在规划层面产生差异的动作头：一个轻量级规划器提出K个潜在规划假设，一个共享的掩码扩散执行器在单次骨干网络前向传播中为每个规划解码一个动作块，策略执行其自身似然排名最高的动作块。这些规划仅从演示中学习，无需规划标签或奖励。在骨干网络、数据和训练方案保持固定的条件下，八个规划条件候选将CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D上的五任务链式成功率从56.9%提升至69.9%，而来自自回归、无规划或同规划重采样的八个候选最多仅达到64.9%。同规划基线是PlanDiv自身检查点在规划固定时的表现，因此这一差距来自规划本身，而非采样数量的增加。在LIBERO-Long上，四个规划消除了40%的单候选失败，而匹配的重采样最多仅消除21%。在真实Franka机械臂上，增益出现在任务允许多种解决方案的场景中：在单一解决方案任务上，PlanDiv与单输出OpenVLA-OFT+基线表现相当；在两个具有两种解决方案的任务上，PlanDiv在54次试验中成功51次，而基线为54次中成功40次。
tldr: PlanDiv improves test-time scaling for VLA models by introducing an action head that proposes diverse latent plan hypotheses, enabling plan-conditioned action candidates that outperform noise-based resampling across CALVIN, LIBERO, and real-robot tasks.
tldr_zh: PlanDiv 通过引入一种动作头来提出多样化的潜在计划假设，使计划条件下的动作候选优于基于噪声的重采样，在 CALVIN、LIBERO 和真实机器人任务上均取得更好表现。

title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
summary: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. Project page: https://movicproject.github.io/ .
summary_zh: 从单目视频中进行实时全身模仿需要同时具备强健的通用追踪器与高质量实时重建能力。我们提出了MoViC框架，该框架利用实时RGB视频作为人形机器人的控制信号，无需佩戴式追踪设备。该框架结合了单目人体运动重建、机器人重定向以及基于Transformer的行为基础模型。策略接收本体感觉历史、单一显式的下一步参考，以及一种紧凑的频域运动表示，该表示在无需显式堆叠未来参考帧的情况下提供时间上下文，从而降低了输入维度和网络规模。在部署阶段，我们的外推方法将10Hz的视觉估计与50Hz的控制器相衔接，实现了视觉处理与策略执行的异步运行。硬件实验进一步展示了从实时单目RGB输入进行高动态运动跟踪以及双臂和单臂操作任务的无设备遥操作。项目页面：https://movicproject.github.io/。
tldr: MoViC is a framework for real-time whole-body control of humanoid robots from monocular video, combining monocular motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model, demonstrated in hardware experiments for dynamic tracking and device-free teleoperation.
tldr_zh: MoViC是一个从单目视频实时控制人形机器人全身的框架，结合了单目运动重建、机器人重定向和基于Transformer的行为基础模型，并在硬件实验中展示了动态跟踪和无设备遥操作。

title: Practice Is Not Free: Measuring the Embodied Cost of Reset-Free Robot Practice
summary: When a robot practices without human resets, every attempt still costs wall-clock time, actuator wear, and sometimes a person's attention, yet the schedulers that decide what to practice next treat attempts as free. We present an open, low-cost testbed for measuring these costs: a self-built SO-101 arm runs two demonstration-trained ACT policies that reset each other, with a vision-based success detector and a ledger that records the time, joint travel, and human interventions of every attempt. We formulate cost-aware practice scheduling, in which task selection is rewarded by measured competence gain net of embodied cost, and specify in advance the comparison that will test it. Its first two conditions, run on hardware for 51 minutes of robot time, show that a fixed retry limit did not reduce the share of execution time lost to failures (36%, against 27% for a feasibility rule; not significant) and saved no robot time. The logs suggest why: failures showed no sign of clustering, so a retry right after a failure was as likely to succeed as any other attempt. The ledger also shows that most of the retry rule's extra human time came from cubes knocked out of reach rather than from the rule itself, and a cost-aware rule replayed on the logs recovers the sensible choice without a hand-set limit. We also report lessons from building the system, including a coverage effect in which concentrating demonstrations in a smaller workspace raised success there from 8/20 to 10/10.
summary_zh: 当机器人在没有人工重置的情况下进行练习时，每一次尝试仍然会消耗实际时间、造成执行器磨损，有时还需要人的关注，然而决定接下来练习什么的调度器却将尝试视为免费的。我们提出了一个开放、低成本的测试平台来衡量这些成本：一个自行搭建的SO-101机械臂运行两个经过演示训练的ACT策略，它们相互重置，并配备基于视觉的成功检测器以及一个台账，记录每一次尝试的时间、关节行程和人工干预。我们制定了成本感知的练习调度方案，其中任务选择以测得的胜任力增益减去具身成本作为奖励依据，并事先明确将要检验该方案的对比实验。其前两个条件在硬件上运行了51分钟的机器人时间，结果显示，固定的重试限制并未降低因失败而损失的执行时间比例（36%，而可行性规则为27%；差异不显著），也没有节省机器人时间。日志揭示了原因：失败没有表现出聚集迹象，因此失败后立即重试的成功概率与其他任何尝试相同。台账还显示，重试规则带来的额外人工时间大部分来自被撞出可及范围的立方体，而非规则本身；将一条成本感知规则在日志上回放，无需手动设定限制即可恢复合理的选择。我们还报告了构建该系统过程中的经验教训，包括一种覆盖效应：将演示集中在较小的操作空间内，使该空间内的成功率从8/20提高到10/10。
tldr: This paper introduces a low-cost testbed for measuring the embodied costs of reset-free robot practice and evaluates cost-aware scheduling rules on a real robot arm, finding that fixed retry limits do not improve efficiency and that failures do not cluster.
tldr_zh: 本文介绍了一个用于测量无重置机器人练习的具身成本的低成本测试平台，并在真实机器人臂上评估了成本感知调度规则，发现固定重试限制不能提高效率，且失败不会聚集。

title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
summary: Autonomous vehicle (AV) decisions at intersections affect the delay, braking, and motion smoothness of surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Learning socially compatible behavior requires connecting imagined interaction outcomes with feedback from executed actions. We propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden. An interaction-aware latent model supports imagination, while off-policy correction and replay updates enable observed rewards and transitions to supervise both the critic and actor. Simulation experiments at an unsignalized intersection achieve a 100% success and reductions in following-HDV acceleration variation of 65.5% and 44.0% relative to PIWM and DreamerV3, respectively. Ablations identify complementary roles for value calibration in reducing HDV burden and policy calibration in improving passage efficiency. Tests under out-of-distribution traffic shifts further show lower ego jerk and HDV acceleration variation than PIWM at comparable passage times.
summary_zh: 自动驾驶车辆（AV）在路口的决策会影响周围人工驾驶车辆（HDVs）的延误、制动及行驶平顺性。学习具有社会兼容性的行为需要将设想的交互结果与实际执行动作后的反馈联系起来。我们提出了一种世界模型强化学习框架，将想象中的策略改进与来自最终交互的直接价值和策略校准相结合，从而在自动驾驶车辆通行效率与HDV交互负担之间取得平衡。该框架中的交互感知潜在模型支持想象过程，而离策略校正与回放更新则利用观测到的奖励和状态转移对评论家网络和行动者网络进行监督。在无信号交叉口的仿真实验中，该方法实现了100%的成功率，并且与PIWM和DreamerV3相比，跟驰HDV加速度变化分别降低了65.5%和44.0%。消融实验揭示了价值校正在减轻HDV负担及策略校正在提升通行效率方面的互补作用。在分布外交通流变化条件下的测试进一步表明，与PIWM相比，本方法在相近通行时间下实现了更低的自我车辆冲击度和HDV加速度变化。
tldr: This paper proposes a world-model reinforcement learning framework that calibrates value and policy from execution feedback to learn socially compatible driving behaviors at intersections, achieving high success rates and reduced HDV burden in simulation.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种世界模型强化学习框架，通过执行反馈校准价值和策略，以在交叉路口学习社会兼容驾驶行为，在仿真中实现了高成功率和降低HDV负担。

title: Lao Siji: Adapting openpilot to Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving in Neural Reconstruction
summary: We present Lao Siji, an end-to-end driving policy that ranks third in the 2026 NVIDIA AlpaSim E2E Driving Challenge, ahead of most entries built on foundation models. Instead of training from scratch on a general-purpose vision backbone, we adapt openpilot, an open-source L2 production model. We freeze its vision encoder and fine-tune the policy layers with an ego-state adapter and a route memory. On closed-loop rollouts in neural-reconstructed scenes, we supervise the policy with a privileged map teacher for lateral self-correction and a body-extent loss for road and obstacle clearance, while distilling the base model's remaining outputs to retain car following. Ablations show that self-correction samples carry the gain, while the clearance loss substitutes for them where no teacher exists. Longitudinal safety instead rests on the base model's lead-vehicle estimate behind a rule-based speed layer. Longer training, imitating human logs, and human-log speed targets yield either no measurable gain or adverse effects. Without further training, Lao Siji also places among the leaders on HUGSIM and Odyssey. The final training takes only one GPU-hour and shifts the weights by 3.9% from the shipped model. Code will be released after review.
summary_zh: 我们提出了“老司机”（Lao Siji），一种端到端驾驶策略，在2026年NVIDIA AlpaSim端到端驾驶挑战赛中排名第三，领先于大多数基于基础模型构建的参赛作品。我们并非在通用视觉骨干网络上从头训练，而是适配了openpilot——一个开源的L2级生产模型。我们冻结其视觉编码器，并通过自我状态适配器（ego-state adapter）和路线记忆（route memory）对策略层进行微调。在神经重建场景的闭环仿真测试中，我们利用特权地图教师模型（privileged map teacher）进行横向自校正，并通过车身范围损失函数（body-extent loss）确保道路与障碍物间的安全间距，同时蒸馏基础模型的其余输出以保持跟车能力。消融实验表明，自校正样本带来了性能提升，而在无教师模型存在的情况下，车身范围损失可替代其作用。纵向安全则依赖于基础模型的前车估计，并辅以基于规则的速度层。更长的训练时间、模仿人类日志以及使用人类日志中的速度目标，要么未带来可测量的提升，要么产生负面影响。无需额外训练，“老司机”在HUGSIM和Odyssey基准上也位居前列。最终训练仅消耗一个GPU小时，且相对于出厂模型的权重变化仅为3.9%。代码将在审阅后发布。
tldr: The paper presents Lao Siji, an end-to-end driving policy adapted from openpilot that ranks third in the NVIDIA AlpaSim E2E Driving Challenge, using ego-state adapter, route memory, and a privileged map teacher for lateral self-correction, while retaining longitudinal safety via a rule-based speed layer.
tldr_zh: 本文提出Lao Siji，一种基于openpilot改造的端到端驾驶策略，在NVIDIA AlpaSim E2E驾驶挑战赛中排名第三，通过自我校正训练和车身范围损失提升横向控制，纵向安全则由规则速度层保障。

title: DiffWAM: Learning World Action Model from Consecutive Visual Difference
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as an important paradigm in robot learning, jointly predicting future scene states and robot actions from current observations and instructions. However, future states entangle task-related changes with large amounts of task-irrelevant content, such as static backgrounds, which weakens the model's ability to capture changes relevant to task execution. To address this, we propose Difference World Action Model (DiffWAM), a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework that enhances world representations by jointly learning future-state prediction and consecutive visual difference prediction. We define consecutive visual differences as differences between the latent representations of consecutive observations, providing an explicit learning signal for temporal variation. The framework comprises a World Expert for future frame prediction, an Action Expert for action generation, and a Diff Expert for predicting these latent differences along the trajectory. A structured unidirectional attention mask conditions the Diff, World, and Action Experts solely on the current-frame representation while blocking attention between experts. This design allows both the World and Diff Experts to be removed during inference, introducing no additional inference overhead. DiffWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on the LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks and substantially improves over FastWAM on real-world manipulation tasks. Specifically, it attains average success rates of 98.8%, 92.65%, and 88.3%, outperforming the state-of-the-art baseline (i.e., FastWAM) by 1.75, 1.55, and 15.0 percentage points, respectively.
summary_zh: 世界动作模型（WAMs）已成为机器人学习中的重要范式，能够根据当前观测和指令联合预测未来场景状态与机器人动作。然而，未来状态将任务相关变化与大量任务无关内容（如静态背景）纠缠在一起，削弱了模型捕捉与任务执行相关变化的能力。为解决这一问题，我们提出差分世界动作模型（DiffWAM），一种专家混合（MoE）框架，通过联合学习未来状态预测与连续视觉差分预测来增强世界表征。我们将连续视觉差分定义为相邻观测潜在表征之间的差异，为时间变化提供显式学习信号。该框架包含用于未来帧预测的世界专家、用于动作生成的动作专家，以及用于沿轨迹预测这些潜在差异的差分专家。一种结构化的单向注意力掩码使差分专家、世界专家和动作专家仅以当前帧表征为条件，同时阻断专家间的注意力流动。这一设计使得世界专家和差分专家在推理时均可被移除，不引入任何额外推理开销。DiffWAM在LIBERO和RoboTwin 2.0基准测试上取得了最先进的结果，并在真实世界操作任务上显著超越FastWAM。具体而言，其平均成功率分别达到98.8%、92.65%和88.3%，较最先进基线（即FastWAM）分别高出1.75、1.55和15.0个百分点。
tldr: DiffWAM introduces a Mixture-of-Experts world action model that jointly predicts future visual states, latent visual differences, and robot actions, improving task-relevant change capture and achieving state-of-the-art performance on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks and real-world manipulation.
tldr_zh: DiffWAM 提出了一种基于混合专家的世界动作模型，通过联合预测未来视觉状态、潜在视觉差异和机器人动作，增强了任务相关变化的捕获能力，在 LIBERO、RoboTwin 2.0 基准和真实世界操作任务中取得了最先进性能。

title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
summary: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.
summary_zh: 联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）世界模型预测未来嵌入而非像素，并在潜在空间中进行规划。仍存在两个挑战：二维图像使得操作所依赖的度量几何变得隐式且与外观纠缠在一起，并且这些模型所想象的内容仍然不可见，因为它们大多在模拟中通过短时程潜在规划进行评估。我们提出了JEPA4R，一种JEPA世界模型，它观测单深度相机点云，在其潜在空间中进行预测和规划，并通过策略头在其冻结的潜在表示上执行动作；我们称之为4D点规划。冻结世界模型上的解码器将其想象的内容以4D点云的形式呈现，200步内的平均点误差在1.1厘米以内。在OGBench和CortexBench的策略学习协议下，JEPA4R在OGBench的Cube-Single、Cube-Double、Cube-Triple和Scene任务上领先于像素JEPA模型，并在MetaWorld和Adroit Relocate任务上以98.4%和88.0%的成绩排名第一，高于亚军R3M的96.0%和65.3%。仅在数字孪生环境中训练的JEPA4R及其策略头可在真实机械臂上以零样本方式运行，同时支持夹爪和灵巧手。
tldr: JEPA4R is a JEPA world model that operates on single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in latent space, and generates 4D point cloud predictions. It outperforms pixel-based JEPA models on various benchmarks and demonstrates zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for real robot manipulation with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.
tldr_zh: JEPA4R 是一种基于深度点云的 JEPA 世界模型，在潜空间中进行预测和规划，并生成 4D 点云预测。它在多个基准测试中优于基于像素的 JEPA 模型，并展示了在真实机器人上使用夹爪和灵巧手的零样本仿真到现实迁移能力。

title: Early Readability of Trajectory Quality in Diffusion Driving Planners
summary: Diffusion-based driving planners can generate multiple trajectories for the same scene, but these candidates vary in quality. Can their internal states reveal which candidate will be better before denoising is complete? We systematically study this question in three pretrained planners: Alpamayo, ReCogDrive-IL, and HDP, using linear probes to predict final trajectory quality from intermediate states and evaluating candidate ranking and selection on held-out scenes.
