summary: Generative novel view synthesis (NVS) employs a diffusion model to render a static or dynamic scene from a target camera view. Explicit warp methods complete a reprojection of the source with video diffusion models, and implicit methods encode the camera parameters or 3D cues. Both add inference overhead, and the generated layout often drifts from the ground truth. We present WaveView, which injects the warped source into the phase of the initial noise of a pretrained generator. The Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Packet Transform (DT-CWPT) allows local and anisotropic phase injection. The generator is thus constrained less in disoccluded regions and along the epipolar line. WaveView keeps the architecture and adds negligible overhead. On the DL3DV benchmark, it outperforms all baselines in every overlap bin. In the hardest bin, it gains 0.84 dB PSNR on the covisible region over MetaView, which shares its generator, while running 2.1 times faster. For dynamic NVS, fine-tuning AnyView with the same noise raises its zero-shot PSNR on AnyViewBench from 11.58 to 12.35 dB.

title: Weight Space Programming for Vision Language Model Repair
summary: In weight-space programming, a language model edits a network's weights directly, without gradients. We ask what a successful repair of this kind relies on. We plant faults in the weights of two vision-language models, SmolVLM-256M and LFM2-VL-450M, and check each edit made by a coding agent against the original weights. Without being told where to look, the agent finds rescaled projector rows and noise in the vision encoder, infers the unknown scale factors, and returns most or all of the rescaled weights to their exact original values and accuracy to near its original level. These repairs depend on a trace of how the faults were computed. The original weights have 16-bit precision, and faults computed in 32-bit arithmetic leave low bits that only the damaged weights carry, a cue that a real failure need not leave. When we round those bits away, each model answers our test questions as before, but the agent, unaided, no longer repairs either model: on LFM2-VL accuracy recovers by about 4 points, against 17 from the unrounded weights. Marking the damaged weights again in their low bits brings the edits back to them. Rounded weights still hold statistical evidence of the rescaling. On SmolVLM the agent uses it once a sentence in the prompt, which we wrote knowing the fault, names such a statistic; on LFM2-VL, whose scale factors are larger, most sessions find the rescaled rows unaided, but none finds the noise. Swapped rows or columns, which keep the set of stored values, are not found unaided on either model within our budgets. We recommend that studies of weight repair report the number format of the weights and include a rounded control.

title: What Do Learned 3D Models Add to Localization from Posed References?
summary: Localizing a query from a few posed reference images avoids building a 3D point map. We ask what the camera predictions of learned 3D models add to geometric estimation from the same references, and where failures arise. Across eight learned models and variants and five test sets, we compare reference budgets, swap pose components, and intervene on the references a model sees. At fine pose-error thresholds, geometric estimation with one additional reference is significantly more accurate than every model on two references on Cambridge and NAVER B1 and never significantly worse, alone or as a fallback behind a shared acceptance gate; with the same three references, the more accurate approach depends on the scene. The gain from the learned translation magnitude depends on reference selection: it improves seven of the eight models on 12-Scenes with the spread-out pairs we select, but none of the five we test with the two top-ranked retrieved references. Where retrieval also returns references from other locations, at NAVER Gangnam Station, models fail at different stages. A robust alignment brings Pi3X and MapAnything within 3.3 pp of adding references as needed. In controlled tests, aligning on the nearby references largely restores VGGT, Pi3X and MapAnything but not Depth Anything 3, and pose-conditioned Pi3X recovers only if the far poses are masked and left out of its input-pose normalization.

title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
summary: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $φ= 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.

title: What Interpolators Store and What They Express: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Benign Overfitting and Label-Free Model Selection
summary: Overparameterized learners can fit noisy training labels perfectly and still predict well, which neither classical complexity measures nor information-theoretic generalization bounds explain. We develop an information-theoretic framework that separates two things an interpolating learner does with its sample: storage, the information the trained model retains about its training labels, and expression, the information about the sample that reaches its predictions at fresh inputs. We first characterize the ideal model: for a loss l, the least complex l-sufficient representation is the Bayes act, whose entropy is the minimal sufficient complexity; this generalizes, and corrects, an earlier "lossless maximal compression" view of boosting. We then show that every interpolator stores exactly nH(Y|X) bits of label noise, so storage, and bounds built on it (including CMI bounds), cannot tell interpolators apart. Expression can: excess risk is bounded above and below by the expressed information V, the entropy over training samples of the prediction at an input, plus a modal-bias term, exactly so for binary labels. Benign overfitting is therefore vanishing expression, a picture that covers nearest-neighbour rules, averaging, minimum-norm least squares and double descent, and that links V to classical bias-variance decompositions and to model disagreement. Finally, V gives a model-selection criterion that needs no held-out labels. Among overparameterized learners on 15 noisy datasets, V estimated from two disjoint halves has 60% less regret than holdout validation at the same cost and matches 5-fold cross-validation at a quarter of its cost; at matched cost it also beats selection by conditional mutual information. We characterize when it fails and give remedies. Code: https://github.com/nnikolaou/GLMC

title: What Right-Angle Corners Reveal About an Uncalibrated Camera: Convex Cones, Certified Bounds and Identifiability
summary: The corner of a box or a room, where three perpendicular edges meet, appears in an image as three segments meeting at a point. We ask what such junctions reveal about an uncalibrated camera's intrinsic parameters. Each junction is consistent with an explicit convex set of cameras; when only the focal length is unknown, this set is an interval in closed form. These sets are computed from the image alone, so calibrating from many junctions is a convex feasibility problem. Almost every junction bounds the focal length from below; we characterize when one also bounds it from above, and when many junctions determine it exactly. For a known vertex, the bounds can be certified against any bounded error in the measured edge directions.

title: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents
summary: Multimodal language models increasingly answer questions over external documents, exposing them to indirect prompt injection: commands planted in untrusted content to hijack the response. Rendering untrusted content as page images lowers attack success on average, leaving open which injected operations survive rendering, at what utility cost, and whether failed image attacks reflect unread commands or commands read but not followed. We pair text and page-image versions of 191 English question-answering sources across six models, measuring marker appending, answer formatting, and answer replacement alongside clean Question-Answering utility. Rendering reduces append and format execution for every model, yet Qwen3-VL-8B still executes image-borne replacement at 77.96\%. Protection also depends on target type, rendering settings, wording, and repetition, and a search over eight fixed attack candidates largely closes the image deficit in appending and formatting for Qwen and Gemini, though not for GPT-5-nano. Utility ratios on original questions range from 93.31\% to 101.61\%, but Qwen falls to 61.99\% when answers combine two evidence spans. Illegibility cannot explain all failed attacks: models often transcribe and identify image-borne commands they do not execute, and trusted user authorization raises execution on unchanged pages. Inside Qwen, patching early attack-region states induces all three operations, more weakly in images. Attention blocking suggests why: a text command acts through its own positions, whereas visual encoding spreads an image command and its target across the instruction page. Rendering thus offers conditional protection, motivating evaluations that report security by model, operation, and attack budget alongside utility.

title: What the model knows but does not say: monitoring medical LLMs through verbalized thoughts
summary: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. Here we show that the model's own internal state, rendered in plain language, exposes manipulations the output conceals. Using a natural-language autoencoder, we translate the activations of a multimodal LLM (Gemma-3-27B) into text and let an input-blind judge read this verbalized internal state (the thoughts channel) and the model's answer separately. Across two clinical attack objectives (omitting a pathology, covertly recommending a drug), two input modalities, and two delivery mechanisms, the thoughts channel caught the injection significantly more often than the answer in all eight injected conditions (p<0.05), while both channels held near-zero false-positive rates on clean inputs; the omission result carried over to Llama-3.3-70B. The thoughts channel also registered unsafe clinical requests as harmful while the model was still reading them, before it decided whether to refuse. None of this requires retraining: an off-the-shelf verbalizer and a general-purpose judge are enough.

title: When Do LLMs Model the Right Target? Problem Formulation in High-Stakes Risk Prediction
summary: Generative AI is increasingly used to assist with data science tasks, yet fundamental questions remain about its ability to correctly formulate analytical problems. We investigate how well large language models (LLMs) can formulate prediction problems when developing models for high-stakes decision making. We focus on one particular challenge to validity: decision dependency, which arises when historical decisions affect observed outcomes. We evaluate this aspect of problem formulation in LLM-generated code and explanations across child-welfare, healthcare, and employment settings, using 11 models from OpenAI and Anthropic and seven prompt conditions. We assess whether the LLM-generated code implements a procedure appropriate for estimating the intended outcome under the study's assumptions and whether the explanation acknowledges decision dependency. We find that LLMs do not reliably address decision dependency without guidance in the prompt. When prompts specify the target, the assumption needed to estimate it, and the estimation procedure, target-aligned implementation reaches 99-100%. Among frontier models, a simple prompt description of how decisions affect outcomes appears sufficient to elicit target-aligned implementation. Some responses also acknowledge decision dependency without addressing it in their code. Our findings suggest that analysts should not rely on LLMs to correctly formulate prediction problems without explicit methodological guidance and careful review. We propose validity-centered guidelines for LLM-assisted predictive modeling, covering prompt formulation, validation of the target and estimation procedure, and identification of key assumptions. Establishing validity is a necessary early step in evaluating whether to deploy a predictive model in a high-stakes setting, but deployment requires weighing broader ethical, institutional, and practical considerations.

title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? A Controlled Study of Dialectal Adaptation for Québec French
summary: Continual pre-training (CPT) is widely used to adapt pretrained language models to dialectal and non-standard language varieties, yet it remains unclear when this additional training is necessary, what drives its benefits, and whether aggregate evaluation scores adequately capture its effects. In this paper, we present a controlled study of CPT for Québec French language understanding across nine LLMs spanning different families and scales. Using a budget-matched protocol of 30M tokens per experiment, our results show that the benefit of CPT depends strongly on the starting model's existing competence in the target variety. When CPT is beneficial, the improvements are driven more by corpus composition than by data volume, with literary text accounting for most of the gain. Paired Québec and standard French evaluations further show that CPT primarily improves expression comprehension rather than grammatical competence, and that corpus register determines which regional expressions are acquired. These gains also involve capability-specific trade-offs, including declines in reading comprehension that aggregate scores can conceal. Overall, these findings show that CPT for dialectal adaptation should not be treated as a uniformly beneficial default. Instead, adaptation strategies should begin with a careful assessment of the base model's existing competence, accompanied by source-level data analysis and task-level evaluation.

title: When Does Subspace Direction Matter for LoRA? Regime Analysis of the Magnitude Principle in Few-Shot Adaptation
summary: We show that the importance of a LoRA adapter's initial input-subspace direction is regime-dependent, and we characterize this dependence in theory and experiment. This refines the recent view that spectral initializers help through update magnitude alone. Direction matters most when labeled data are scarce relative to the representation dimension and the activation subspace used for initialization captures supervised task structure. In this regime, the adapter's row span remains sensitive to its starting point, making task-aligned initialization especially useful. A spiked-covariance perturbation analysis characterizes the finite-sample stability of the estimated subspace. A first-step analysis of LoRA training explains why the subspace's alignment with the task matters and motivates an alignment coefficient $ρ$ that closely tracks gains across classification tasks. We test this account with PivotLoRA, which initializes adapters from activation PCA at prediction-relevant positions and applies one output-preserving orthogonal pivot early in training. In few-shot BERT-base classification, PivotLoRA achieves the best average rank among 13 methods and improves over vanilla LoRA in 29 of 30 settings, even though it starts from a smaller input-factor initialization norm. Additional classification experiments extend the evaluation to 7B and 8B Llama decoders. Classification gains diminish with more labeled data, consistent with the proposed regime dependence. A targeted extension to completion-only reasoning also shows improvements on GSM8K and StrategyQA. These findings identify conditions under which initialization direction matters, with subspace-task alignment offering a low-cost diagnostic before training for classification.

title: When Figures Disagree with Text: Evaluating Autonomous Visual Evidence Verification in Scientific Papers
summary: Scientific figures carry evidence for the claims that cite them, so reviewing a paper means checking that a figure agrees with the text, and not only describing what the figure shows. Benchmarks of figure-text verification typically hand the model the figure, the claim, or the knowledge that an inconsistency exists, which leaves untested whether a model can find the figure worth checking in a complete paper, relate a visual element to the claim it conflicts with, and recognize the conflict. We study this autonomous setting on 31 full manuscripts, each carrying a reviewer-documented figure-text inconsistency from PRISMM-Bench that is hidden from the model. Six multimodal models review each PDF under a neutral prompt, and we then add one input at a time to the same manuscripts. Of 1,445 open-ended reviews, 60.6% mention the flawed figure, yet a grading rubric accepts only 3.3% as diagnosing its contradiction; a blind audit finds the rubric lenient, so we read these as rubric-accepted rates and compare conditions rather than absolute values. In a separate controlled run, naming the figure, without stating that it is flawed, raises rubric-accepted diagnosis from 4.3% to 20.4%, while a consistency instruction and coarse visual cues do not. When the contradiction is visible only in the rendered figure, text-only review yields no accepted diagnosis, while review of the rendered pages with the figure named reaches 15.8%. A baseline that lets the model choose which figures to check, ranked by centrality, stays at 4.8%. Deciding what to verify is thus a large part of the difficulty, and the selection rule we tested does not resolve it. Multimodal document understanding should be evaluated on whether a model can propose what to verify, not only answer questions about a figure it is handed.

title: When Normal-Only Updates Are Not Enough: Test-Time Adaptation in Reconstruction-Based Time-Series Anomaly Detection
summary: Normal operating conditions can evolve after deployment, motivating test-time adaptation (TTA) of time-series anomaly detectors using incoming data. Yet the same stream may contain anomalies, so TTA with online updates must decide which test samples should be used for adaptation. This leaves a more basic question: even if updates are restricted to samples labeled as normal in the benchmark, does TTA reliably improve anomaly detection? We study this question with a controlled intervention that replaces the practical update selector with a rule that uses only samples labeled as normal in the benchmark, while keeping the rest of the online adaptation procedure unchanged. Across nine benchmark families, four optimizer configurations, and five random seeds, we obtain three main findings: (1) using only samples labeled as normal in the benchmark does not reliably improve detection; (2) practical TTA failures exhibit two distinct responses to this intervention, with 63 of 180 settings recovering a clear detection gain while 90 still show no clear detection gain; and (3) the updates reduce their immediate reconstruction objective across the evaluated settings, yet these reductions do not consistently lead to better anomaly ranking. Both failure patterns persist across alternative practical adaptation variants and modest perturbations of the benchmark labels. Together, these findings show that improving sample selection alone is not a complete solution to reconstruction-based TSAD TTA.

title: When accuracy hides risk: risk-controlled confirmation of the critical view of safety under expert disagreement
summary: Automated assessment of the critical view of safety (CVS) in laparoscopic cholecystectomy has advanced rapidly, but a deployed check must decide, before the first clip, whether to confirm CVS. The standard rule calibrates a threshold so that false confirmations are rare on average. We show that this rule concentrates its errors on disputed videos, which one of three expert raters judged sufficient, and that the failure is structural. When reference labels are votes of a panel sampled from a larger expert pool, the rule that maximizes sensitivity at a fixed average false-confirmation rate also maximizes false confirmation of disputed videos, and for recognizers that recover expert judgement with less noise this rate rises with accuracy. We propose certified confirmation, a risk-controlled monitoring rule whose threshold is selected by multiple testing so that, with probability at least 1 - δ, false confirmation is at most α overall, among disputed videos, within vendor and country groups, and before CVS is visible, using disputed labels only to calibrate. In a pre-specified, hash-locked evaluation on the 300 test videos (18 countries) of the SAGES CVS Challenge, standard calibration falsely confirmed 8 of 39 disputed videos (0.21; one-sided p = 0.037 against α = 0.10), whereas certified confirmation confirmed 2 (one-sided 95% upper bound 0.15). On development data, protection held for vendor and country groups left out of calibration. The cost was confirming 10% rather than 35% of sufficient videos on time. Average accuracy hides this risk; disputed cases must be protected explicitly.

title: Where Global Context and Weight Sharing Work in Compact Vision Backbones
summary: Compact convolutional backbones such as EfficientNet achieve strong parameter efficiency through local depthwise separable convolutions, yet two structural questions remain central to hybrid design: where does global self-attention improve recognition over pure convolution, and can repeated blocks share weights without losing representational capacity? We investigate both questions on ImageNet-1k (50,000-image validation) using controlled EfficientNet-B0 experiments. First, we show that wrapping a classification backbone in multi-scale feature pyramids (BiFPN) fails to outperform a plain MBConv trunk (69.99% - 71.81% vs. 72.86% plain B0) until paired with stage attention (73.15%). In contrast, keeping the MBConv trunk intact and inserting lightweight zero-gated residual self-attention adapters at stages P3 (28x28 windowed), P4 (14x14 global), and P5 (7x7 global) reaches 74.02% standalone and outperforms a bit-for-bit matched plain-B0 control by +0.954 percentage points (73.88% vs. 72.92%) across an 88-epoch stateless replay schedule, with learned attention amplitude rising monotonically with semantic depth (27.2% at P3 -> 45.4% at P4 -> 66.3% at P5). Second, we evaluate recurrent weight sharing across repeated MBConv blocks with pass-specific BatchNorm statistics (+1,536 parameters per pass). While post-hoc kernel averaging degrades accuracy to 17.03% and single-template stage tying (-27.6% parameters) plateaus at 66.10%, alternating two shared block templates ([B1, A, B, A]) in Stage 6 cuts total model parameters by 10.9% (582K weights) and recovers by +10.82 points in a single epoch to 70.92% (-1.84 points vs. unshared control).

title: Where Should a Diffusion Transformer Meet Its Teacher?
summary: Representation Alignment (REPA) significantly accelerates Diffusion Transformer training by guiding intermediate student features with a pretrained visual teacher, yet existing methods typically attach supervision to a single fixed layer. As student representations evolve, however, we find that the most effective layer for alignment varies across training stages. To track this evolving layer suitability online without costly search, we measure gradient compatibility between the flow-matching and alignment objectives, and propose AdaREPA, an online routing framework that adaptively selects the supervision layer as training progresses. AdaREPA uses a softmax distribution over smoothed layer compatibility scores to sample a layer for alignment at each training step. This probabilistic routing adapts teacher supervision to the student's changing learning needs, with minimal training overhead and no additional inference cost. On ImageNet-256, AdaREPA accelerates convergence and improves generation quality across model sizes, while revealing how the most suitable layers for supervision shift over training.

title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
summary: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. The cycle returns the requested edits to where they began, with each direction started from a stored reference tree, and the spread of its cost over repeated cycles defines a software temperature, which rose with the sampling temperature of the model. About 80 per cent of the tokens of a successful run are generated in model calls that leave the requested change where it was, and we call these tokens heat. The free energy of a change, which we estimate by analogy with the equality of Jarzynski, is 14 to 22 per cent of the mean cost of a successful coding run. Coding costs 1.1 to 1.5 times as much as uncoding. The daemon is imperfect: the verdict of a test suite varies with its environment, and a suite that accepts a broken change has a cost in tokens. The practical implication of the proposed theory could be new tools for analysing and optimising coding agents through the lens of thermodynamics.

title: Which Tokens, in What Order, and How Fast? A Theoretical Analysis of On-Policy Distillation Objectives
summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model to match a teacher model based on its own generations. When using OPD, one must choose whether to apply it at the sequence or token level and which divergence to minimize. However, despite the wide adoption of OPD in practice, the formal understanding of which OPD objective is appropriate for a given setting is limited. Toward addressing this gap, we theoretically analyze how the choice of OPD objective governs which tokens are prioritized, in what order, and how efficiently. Our analysis reveals that sequence-level OPD exhibits a future agreement bias, which myopic token-level objectives avoid. This bias induces a reverse learning order, in which sequence-level OPD first matches the teacher at later token positions, while at earlier positions it can favor tokens that are improbable under the teacher, and thus often undesirable. As for the choice of divergence, we prove that it strongly influences the amenability of OPD to gradient-based optimization. In particular, while the forward KL divergence enjoys a well-behaved objective landscape, other $f$-divergences, such as reverse KL, can suffer from vanishing gradients even when the student and teacher are far apart. Across language model post-training settings, we demonstrate the implications of these theoretical findings for which OPD objective is preferable, highlighting the importance of accounting for the interplay between the student, teacher, and task at hand.

title: Why Multi-Source Audio Fails to Compose: A Geometric Diagnosis and Its Remedy
summary: Multi-source audio-to-image generation exhibits consistent compositional failures when audio tokens occupy geometrically displaced, semantically unanchored positions in the CLIP text-token space, where the diffusion U-Net lacks the prior to reliably attend to them or ground them in distinct spatial regions. We formalize this as the geometric displacement phenomenon and expose it through a two-level clustering analysis comparing BEATs and CLAP embeddings at the raw encoder and projected CLIP token levels. Three geometric properties emerge as important: intra-class compactness, angular alignment with the CLIP text manifold, and inter-token spatial separation. We show that CLAP, whose contrastive language-audio pretraining aligns embeddings with natural language semantics, substantially outperforms BEATs on all three properties, improving the silhouette score by more than 3x and the Audio-Image Content score as well. Building on this analysis, we introduce a multi-token extension that requires no diffusion-backbone retraining and assigns each audio source to a distinct placeholder token in the CLIP tokenizer, complemented by a mixed inference-time objective that combines Attend-and-Excite with an A* spatial separation loss to resolve residual cross-token interference. For evaluation, we construct multi-audio compositional benchmarks from VGGSound (VGG2, VGG3, and VGGN) and extend six standard audio-image metrics to the multi-source setting. Across five benchmarks and four strong baselines, our method achieves strong results on the metrics most directly tied to compositional faithfulness, with AIC improvements of up to 2.25x over the strongest baseline and FID reduced by nearly 2x on two-source generation. We propose geometric displacement as a diagnostic framework for cross-modal generation systems that project learned embeddings into a pretrained contrastive space.

title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
summary: Deep vision models operating in resource-constrained environments depend heavily on low-bit quantization, yet compressing weights below 4 bits frequently induces catastrophic accuracy collapse. While mixed-precision recovery strategies aim to rescue accuracy by selectively retaining high-precision parameters, the fundamental mechanics of where and why these models collapse remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically analyze the anatomy of quantization collapse across standard Vision CNNs (including ResNet and EfficientNet backbones) evaluated on the full 50,000-image ImageNet-1k validation set. First, we map the exact progression of degradation, demonstrating that collapse is highly non-linear and concentrated in late-stage pointwise projections and depthwise layers. Second, we introduce a structured, multi-step recovery waterfall that evaluates selective integer precision (INT4/INT8) and selective floating-point scales. We show that keeping less than 5% of critical layer activations in 8-bit precision recovers up to 92% of the accuracy lost during aggressive sub-4-bit compression. Finally, we bridge the hardware reality gap by evaluating deployment performance on standard ARM and x86 CPU architectures. We show that while low-bit quantization reduces memory storage requirements, standard runtime software bit-unpacking introduces a 1.48x to 21.5x execution slowdown depending on batch size, highlighting a critical trade-off between model footprint and actual edge throughput. Our findings provide a practical blueprint for navigating the limits of sub-4-bit deployment without sacrificing hardware performance.

title: Zonotopic Analysis of Quantization Error in Neural Networks
summary: Quantized neural networks achieve computational efficiency by reducing precision, but bounding their quantization error remains a challenge due to discrete rounding and clamping operations. We present a zonotope-based abstract interpretation framework for quantized ReLU feed-forward network verification, introducing a unified round-clamp abstract transformer that jointly handles both operations. We extend this framework to constrained zonotopes, which add linear constraints to tighten bounds, and derive sound quantization error representations. We establish soundness and affine-strip optimality of the round-clamp abstract transformer, as well as convex-hull optimality of its complete constrained formulation. On the ACAS Xu benchmarks, our constrained zonotope method reduces average error-bound widths by approximately 70-85% and runtimes by 65-80% compared to QEBVerif's symbolic DRA propagation at the two smallest tested perturbation radii (r=3 and r=6). These improvements are not uniform across bitwidths, and symbolic DRA achieves tighter bounds at larger radii. Our plain zonotope method delivers competitive sound bounds nearly 300 times faster on average.

title: automodel: A Skill for Agentic Model Discovery
summary: The search for better models, whether expressed as analytical equations or neural architectures, has increasingly shifted from manual design toward data-driven automation. While a multitude of algorithms exist, ranging from exhaustive search to AlphaEvolve, recent advances in general-purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex raise the question: could providing such systems with a "model discovery recipe" be enough to discover or improve models? We present automodel, an agent skill for general model discovery. With case studies in astrophysics, cardiovascular dynamics, precision agriculture, traffic flow, and vehicle tire dynamics, we show how commercial agents equipped with automodel can successfully identify novel and scientifically-relevant models. Our findings suggest that encoding model-discovery methodology as a portable agent skill can provide a simple, interactive, powerful and broadly applicable alternative to domain-specific automated discovery pipelines. The skill is available at: https://github.com/unlayer-ai/automodel.

title: mmTherm: Absolute 3D Human Pose Estimation from Low-Resolution Thermal Images and mmWave Radar
summary: Absolute 3D human pose estimation (HPE) aims to recover both a person's body pose and their global position in 3D space. Privacy-preserving millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides distance and direction measurement capabilities, but its sparse point clouds make HPE under-constrained. Low-resolution thermal imaging can provide complementary observations of body direction and structure. However, our evaluation shows that a strong feature-level fusion baseline loses much of its localization and HPE advantage when generalizing to unseen subjects, with radial localization becoming less accurate than a radar-only baseline. Motivated by this finding, we introduce mmTherm, a lightweight framework that explicitly incorporates the complementary geometric properties of thermal imaging and mmWave radar. It combines body structure and joint directions estimated from thermal images with range information from radar to localize the body and reconstruct its 3D pose. Experiments on OctoNet show that mmTherm reduces cross-user absolute joint error by 33% and root localization error by 38% relative to the strongest corresponding baselines, while requiring substantially fewer parameters and less computation at inference.

title: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience
summary: A central goal of humanoid robotics is for robots to perform the everyday work people do in homes and workplaces. Existing egocentric video datasets cover many of these activities but provide little synchronized whole-body motion data for learning loco-manipulation at scale. We build Awaken-Human, which pairs approximately 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body human motion and covers more than 100 skills. Building on this, we also introduce Awaken-HI (Humanoid Intelligence), a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert. We show that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert. Increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks. After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, Awaken-HI achieves a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight individual tasks and outperforms GR00T N1.7 and $π_{0.5}$ in both individual and long-horizon evaluations. The same policy generalizes to objects unseen during robot post-training and to new pairings of familiar objects and destinations.
summary_zh: 构建人形机器人领域的核心目标之一，是使机器人能够执行人们在家庭和工作场所中的日常工作任务。现有的大规模自我中心视频数据集涵盖了许多此类活动，但为学习移动操作任务提供的人体全身同步运动数据却相对匮乏。为此，我们构建了Awaken-Human数据集，该数据集包含约5万小时的自我中心立体视频，并与全身人体运动数据同步，覆盖了超过100种技能。在此基础上，我们进一步推出了Awaken-HI（人形智能），这是一个专为人形机器人移动操作设计的视觉-语言-动作模型，通过共享动作专家模块，能够同时预测原始人体运动和重定向后的机器人动作。研究表明，当人体运动轨迹直接监督共享动作专家模块时，人形机器人的移动操作技能从人类到机器人的迁移效果更为显著。经验缩放定律显示，增加人类预训练数据量能够降低保留机器人动作预测误差，并提升下游真实机器人任务的平均成功率。在完成全语料库预训练及T800适配后，Awaken-HI在八项单独任务中平均成功率达到93.75%，在单独任务及长时程任务评估中均优于GR00T N1.7和π0.5。该策略同样能够泛化至机器人后训练阶段未见过的物体，以及熟悉物体与目的地的新组合。
tldr: This paper introduces Awaken-Human, a large-scale dataset of 50,000 hours of egocentric video with synchronized whole-body human motion, and Awaken-HI, a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that uses human trajectories to supervise a shared action expert, achieving high success on real-robot tasks.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了Awaken-Human，一个包含5万小时第一视角视频与同步全身人体运动的大规模数据集，并基于此训练了Awaken-HI，一种通过共享动作专家利用人体轨迹监督人形机器人操作与移动的视觉-语言-动作模型，在真实机器人任务上取得了高成功率。

title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型近来已结合触觉感知技术，以在接触密集的操作任务中感知视觉上难以察觉的接触事件。然而，加入触觉输入所带来的性能提升并不稳定，部分视觉-触觉VLA模型对触觉输入的依赖程度较低，原因在于大量触觉变化（如夹爪闭合过程中的凝胶形变）可通过视觉观察及已执行的动作加以预测。为解决这一问题，我们提出了TacInno，该方法将视觉与已执行动作无法解释的接触动态分离出来，称之为触觉创新信息，并仅将触觉创新信息作为训练目标。具体而言，TacInno分词器以视觉观察和已执行动作为条件，将未来的触觉变化压缩为离散编码，而策略模型TacInno-VLA则学习预测该编码，在部署时无需额外引入任何编码模块。TacInno-VLA在六个模拟任务中平均成功率达到87.5%，在四个真实世界任务中平均成功率达到70.5%，分别比最强的视觉-触觉基线方法高出10.7和9.0个百分点。消融研究验证了视觉与动作条件建模、多帧编码以及辅助编码预测的各自贡献。综合以上结果，充分证明了触觉创新信息作为接触密集操作监督信号的有效性。
tldr: TacInno introduces a method to isolate and use tactile innovation—contact dynamics unexplained by vision and actions—as a training target for VLA models, improving contact-rich manipulation performance across simulation and real-world tasks.
tldr_zh: TacInno 提出了一种方法，将视觉和动作无法解释的触觉创新（接触动力学）作为 VLA 模型的训练目标，从而提升了接触丰富操作任务在仿真和真实世界中的性能。

title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. While prior work has explored task suppression and refusal, stopping prohibited behavior once execution is underway and controlling the resulting physical response remain challenging. Our evaluation reveals that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution. Even when the task remains unfinished, the robot may drop a held object, making non-completion an incomplete measure of safety. To address these challenges, we introduce State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) for tasks where holding provides an appropriate alternative response. SAFI comprises two stages, (1) fallback target construction, which assigns stationary arm commands and consistent gripper targets throughout prohibited-task demonstrations, and (2) joint policy adaptation, which learns these targets alongside the original actions of retained tasks. This supervision teaches an explicit alternative response at intermediate execution states while maintaining the robot's other skills. Extensive experiments with OpenVLA-OFT across LIBERO and BadLIBERO tasks evaluate prohibited completion, physical incidents, and retained-task performance. On the evaluated LIBERO tasks, SAFI reduces aggregate target success after takeover to 1.3\%, with no recorded physical incidents or action saturation, while preserving high retained-task success.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-行动（VLA）模型使机器人能够根据视觉观察和语言指令执行多种任务。尽管已有研究探讨了任务抑制与拒绝，但在执行过程中阻止违禁行为并控制由此产生的物理响应仍然具有挑战性。我们的评估表明，能够从初始状态抑制任务的策略，在任务执行中途接管时仍可能完成任务。即使任务未完成，机器人也可能掉落手中物体，使得“未完成”这一指标不足以全面衡量安全性。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了状态感知回退模仿（SAFI），适用于“握持”可作为合理替代响应的任务。SAFI包含两个阶段：（1）回退目标构建，在违禁任务示范中分配静止的机械臂指令和一致的夹爪目标；（2）联合策略适配，在保留任务原始动作的同时学习这些目标。该监督方式在中间执行状态下教授显式的替代响应，同时保持机器人的其他技能。我们在LIBERO和BadLIBERO任务上使用OpenVLA-OFT进行了大量实验，评估了违禁任务完成率、物理事故及保留任务性能。在所评估的LIBERO任务中，SAFI将接管后的综合目标成功率降至1.3%，且未记录到任何物理事故或动作饱和，同时保持了较高的保留任务成功率。
tldr: This paper proposes State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI), a method for teaching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to stop prohibited tasks safely by learning an alternative holding behavior at intermediate execution states, reducing task completion and physical incidents.
tldr_zh: 本文提出状态感知回退模仿（SAFI），通过在学习中间执行状态下的替代握持行为，教会视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型安全停止被禁止的任务，从而减少任务完成率和物理事故。

title: UniVEP: Unifying Velocity and Endpoint Prediction for Robot Manipulation
summary: Flow-matching robot policies usually use one prediction target throughout action generation, even though recovering actions from noise and polishing nearly clean actions bring different challenges. We systematically compare velocity prediction (V), endpoint prediction (X), and velocity-weighted endpoint prediction (X--V) across multiple robot policies, benchmarks, and inference budgets. On StarVLA and LiLa-WAM, X--V works best for few-step generation, while V gains more from iterative refinement. We further uncover their complementary strengths across noise levels: clean actions have concentrated covariance spectra, endpoint predictions stay more stable under high noise, and velocity predictions offer more accurate corrections near clean actions. Inspired by these findings, we introduce UniVEP, which learns both prediction targets together with consistency supervision and switches from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement as noise drops. Each step only needs one network run, and joint training also boosts single-step endpoint generation. Tests on simulated and real-world manipulation show better success rates and efficiency. On RoboTwin, UniVEP hits 61.36% success with one StarVLA run, beating the best single-target baseline at sixteen runs (59.96%). With LiLa-WAM, two runs outperform the best sixteen-step single-target baseline and cut inference latency by 77.1%.
summary_zh: 流匹配机器人策略通常在动作生成的整个过程中使用单一的预测目标，尽管从噪声中恢复动作与优化近乎干净的动作带来了不同的挑战。我们系统地在多种机器人策略、基准测试和推理预算下比较了速度预测（V）、端点预测（X）以及速度加权端点预测（X--V）。在StarVLA和LiLa-WAM上，X--V在少步生成中表现最佳，而V则更多受益于迭代细化。我们进一步揭示了它们在不同噪声水平下的互补优势：干净动作具有集中的协方差谱，端点预测在高噪声下保持更稳定，而速度预测在接近干净动作时提供更精确的修正。受这些发现的启发，我们提出了UniVEP，该方法同时学习两个预测目标并辅以一致性监督，随着噪声降低，从端点恢复切换至速度细化。每一步仅需一次网络运行，联合训练同时提升了单步端点生成的效果。在仿真和真实世界的操作测试中，UniVEP展现了更高的成功率和效率。在RoboTwin上，UniVEP以单次StarVLA运行达到61.36%的成功率，超过了最佳单目标基线在十六次运行下的表现（59.96%）。使用LiLa-WAM时，两次运行的性能优于最佳十六步单目标基线，并将推理延迟降低了77.1%。
tldr: UniVEP unifies velocity and endpoint prediction targets in flow-matching robot manipulation policies, switching from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement based on noise level, achieving higher success rates and lower latency than single-target baselines in simulated and real-world tests.
tldr_zh: UniVEP在流匹配机器人操作策略中统一了速度与端点预测目标，根据噪声水平从端点恢复切换到速度细化，在模拟和真实测试中取得了更高的成功率和更低的延迟。

title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
summary: Tools with different shapes can have similar functions, but transferring manipulation skills across tools requires understanding how tool geometry relates to the specific task and adjusting the manipulation strategy accordingly. The key challenge is to discover the common affordances that contribute to task completion across different tools and verify whether they support new tools in performing similar work. We present A$^2$-VLA, a tool-adaptation framework that combines an embodied agent with a VLA policy. It treats tool affordances as hypotheses the agent can construct, test, and revise. Given teleoperated demonstrations with a few source tools, the agent reconstructs the scenes in simulation and autonomously determines task-relevant affordance features: functional regions and their key geometric properties. It develops affordance-extraction skills and refines both the features and skills through autonomous experiments in the reconstructed scenes. Validated extraction skills accumulate in a reusable skill library for unseen tools. Finally, A$^2$-VLA uses encoded functional-region features as conditioning inputs to a $π_{0.5}$ backbone during training and inference. Evaluation examines affordance reliability in reconstructed scenes and real-robot task success on unseen tools. Our method achieves 86.1% success in simulated cross-tool trajectory retargeting based on affordances. On three real-robot tool-use tasks, A$^2$-VLA improves task success by 30.7 percentage points over $π_{0.5}$.
summary_zh: 不同形状的工具可能具有相似的功能，但跨工具迁移操作技能需要理解工具几何形状与具体任务之间的关系，并据此调整操作策略。关键挑战在于发现不同工具间有助于任务完成的共同可供性（affordances），并验证这些可供性是否支持新工具执行类似操作。我们提出A$^2$-VLA，一种结合具身智能体与VLA策略的工具适配框架。该框架将工具可供性视为智能体可以构建、测试和修正的假设。给定使用少量源工具的遥操作演示，智能体在仿真中重建场景，并自主确定与任务相关的可供性特征：功能区域及其关键几何属性。它发展出可供性提取技能，并通过在重建场景中的自主实验迭代优化特征与技能。经过验证的提取技能积累到可复用的技能库中，用于处理未见过的工具。最后，A$^2$-VLA在训练和推断阶段将编码后的功能区域特征作为条件输入馈入$π_{0.5}$骨干网络。评估涵盖重建场景中的可供性可靠性以及真实机器人对未见工具的任务成功率。我们的方法在基于可供性的仿真跨工具轨迹重定向上实现了86.1%的成功率。在三个真实机器人工具使用任务中，A$^2$-VLA相比$π_{0.5}$将任务成功率提升了30.7个百分点。
tldr: A^2-VLA is a tool-adaptation framework that uses an embodied agent to discover task-relevant affordances (functional regions and geometric properties) from a few demonstrations, test them in simulation, and condition a VLA policy (π0.5 backbone) on these affordance features, achieving significant real-robot task success improvement on unseen tools.
tldr_zh: A^2-VLA 是一个工具自适应框架，通过具身智能体从少量演示中自主发现任务相关的可供性（功能区域及其几何属性），在仿真中验证，并将这些特征作为条件输入到 VLA 策略（基于 π0.5）中，在未见过的工具上显著提高了真实机器人任务成功率。

title: LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference
summary: World action models (WAMs) couple generative video modeling with robotic action prediction but typically require large video and action transformers, limiting deployment efficiency. We present LoopedWAM, a compact WAM that recurrently applies a shared six-block core in each expert, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert. To account for their asymmetric inference costs, the video and action experts can operate at different depths: visual features are computed once per query, whereas action computation repeats at every sampling step. We further propose elastic self-distillation, which trains a single elastic checkpoint, LoopedWAM-E, across action-depth and sampling-step budgets. With only 0.58B policy parameters and no robot pretraining, LoopedWAM achieves 96.1% success on LIBERO, 91.9% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 52.2% on RoboCasaGR1, while using $7.4\times$ less peak GPU memory than Fast-WAM under matched inference measurements. On LIBERO, LoopedWAM-E achieves 96.0% success in 27.6 ms or 95.2% in 24.7 ms on an H100, providing multiple accuracy-latency operating points from a single checkpoint; with two sampling steps and four action loops, it stays within 0.5 points of LoopedWAM on all three benchmarks. Ablations demonstrate that weight-shared depth preserves competitive performance, while aggressive action-depth reduction requires explicit budget-aware training. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, LoopedWAM succeeds in 71.3% of 80 trials across four tasks.
summary_zh: 世界动作模型（WAMs）将生成式视频建模与机器人动作预测相结合，但通常需要大型视频和动作变换器，限制了部署效率。我们提出LoopedWAM，一种紧凑型WAM，在每个专家中循环应用共享的六块核心，执行30层变换器，而每个专家仅存储12个块。考虑到其非对称推理成本，视频和动作专家可以在不同深度运行：视觉特征每次查询计算一次，而动作计算则在每个采样步骤重复进行。我们进一步提出弹性自蒸馏方法，训练单一弹性检查点LoopedWAM-E，覆盖动作深度和采样步骤预算。仅使用0.58B策略参数且无需机器人预训练，LoopedWAM在LIBERO上达到96.1%的成功率，在RoboTwin 2.0上达到91.9%，在RoboCasaGR1上达到52.2%，同时在匹配推理测量下，峰值GPU内存比Fast-WAM减少7.4倍。在LIBERO上，LoopedWAM-E在H100上以27.6 ms达到96.0%的成功率，或以24.7 ms达到95.2%的成功率，从单一检查点提供多个精度-延迟工作点；使用两个采样步骤和四个动作循环时，在三个基准上与LoopedWAM的差距保持在0.5个百分点以内。消融实验表明，权重共享深度保持了竞争性能，而激进的深度降低则需要显式的预算感知训练。在真实的AgileX PiPER机械臂上，LoopedWAM在四个任务的80次试验中成功率达到71.3%。
tldr: LoopedWAM introduces a weight-shared, elastic world action model that reduces memory and compute for robot manipulation policies by recurrently applying a small transformer core and elastic self-distillation, enabling multiple accuracy-latency trade-offs from a single checkpoint.
tldr_zh: LoopedWAM 提出了一种权重共享且弹性深度的世界动作模型，通过循环应用小型 transformer 核心和弹性自蒸馏，降低机器人操作策略的内存与计算开销，并支持单个检查点下的多种精度-延迟权衡。

title: WEVO: World Model-Enabled VLA Optimization for Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. We present WEVO, a teleoperation-free framework for post-training a whole-body humanoid VLA in an action-conditioned video world model (WM). Simulated manipulation and locomotion play data improve contact-dynamics and viewpoint-change prediction. A VLA trained on synthetic demonstrations collects 20 autonomous real robot rollouts per task to align the WM with deployment observations. The VLA, whole-body controller (WBC), and video WM then form a closed-loop RL environment with dense progress rewards. Across three real robot tasks, play data improves every evaluated WM metric and downstream policy success; video WM RL raises mean success from 23.3% to 75.0%, compared with 48.3% for real robot RL. We therefore leverage the complementary strengths of both environments: simulation provides policy initialization and broad coverage, while the video WM offers a deployment-aligned environment for policy improvement. Project website: https://qianzhong-chen.github.io/wevo.github.io/.
summary_zh: 强化学习（RL）可以超越模仿学习，进一步提升视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略的性能，但人形机器人的探索存在安全风险，且仿真环境中的强化学习可能利用未建模的仿真到现实差距（sim-to-real gaps）。我们提出WEVO，一种无需远程操作的框架，用于在动作条件视频世界模型（WM）中对全身人形VLA进行后训练。模拟操作和移动数据改善了接触动力学和视角变化预测。基于合成演示训练的VLA在每个任务中收集20次自主真实机器人轨迹，以对齐世界模型与实际部署观测。随后，VLA、全身控制器（WBC）和视频世界模型构成闭环强化学习环境，并提供密集进度奖励。在三个真实机器人任务中，操作数据改善了所有评估的世界模型指标及下游策略成功率；视频世界模型强化学习将平均成功率从23.3%提升至75.0%，而真实机器人强化学习仅为48.3%。因此，我们充分利用两种环境的互补优势：仿真提供策略初始化与广泛覆盖，而视频世界模型则提供与部署对齐的策略改进环境。项目网站：https://qianzhong-chen.github.io/wevo.github.io/。
tldr: WEVO post-trains a whole-body humanoid VLA policy in a deployment-aligned action-conditioned video world model, using simulated play data and a closed-loop RL environment to improve real-world loco-manipulation success rates.
tldr_zh: WEVO 在部署对齐的动作条件视频世界模型中后训练全身人形 VLA 策略，利用模拟数据与闭环 RL 环境提升真实世界移动操控成功率。

title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
summary: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present. Coupling a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders. Trained on human video and robot trajectories, $Z$-sight achieves 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points over the strongest baseline) and 73.3% across six Unitree G1 tasks (+20.0 points) at 110 ms per chunk, while remaining competitive on tabletop benchmarks.
summary_zh: 我们提出$Z$-sight，这是一种统一的机器人基础模型，将视觉-语言-动作（VLA）与生成式潜在世界建模相结合。基于视频的世界动作模型（WAMs）展示了联合未来生成与动作生成对控制的价值，但继承了视频生成器的高昂成本。近期的潜在空间策略避免了像素生成，但通常依赖于中间特征对齐或冻结的目标编码器，将未来预测与VLM的原生特征空间割裂开来。$Z$-sight则在其VLM感知当前场景的视觉标记空间中直接预测未来。通过将前瞻专家和连续动作专家与VLM以混合Transformer架构耦合，$Z$-sight在推理时联合去噪未来空间标记和动作，无需像素重建或外部编码器。在人类视频和机器人轨迹上训练后，$Z$-sight在SIMPLE基准上达到81.9%的成功率（比最强基线高出9.6个百分点），在六项Unitree G1任务上平均成功率为73.3%（高出20.0个百分点），每个块的处理时间为110毫秒，同时在桌面操作基准上保持竞争力。
tldr: Z-sight unifies vision-language-action with latent world modeling by jointly predicting future visual tokens and actions in the VLM's token space, avoiding pixel reconstruction, and achieves strong success on SIMPLE and Unitree G1 tasks.
tldr_zh: Z-sight通过直接在VLM的视觉token空间中联合预测未来token和动作，统一了视觉-语言-动作模型与潜在世界模型，避免了像素重建，并在SIMPLE和Unitree G1任务上取得了优异表现。

title: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models
summary: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. To study pretraining data efficiency, we curate approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot manipulation data for representation learning and use the robot demonstration subset for WAM pretraining. Following benchmark-specific post-training, Phoenix achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-robot benchmarks spanning single-arm, bimanual, and dexterous manipulation. It demonstrates strong robustness to perturbations, achieving success rates of 94.8% on LIBERO-Plus and 72.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 C2R, alongside strong cross-embodiment transfer and real-world manipulation performance on Bench2Dex and RoboDojo-RealWorld, respectively. Pretraining-scale analysis shows larger performance gains from data scaling than a video-VAE-only baseline, indicating stronger scaling benefits and more effective data utilization. Moreover, Phoenix maintains high success rates when adapted with limited downstream demonstrations, demonstrating strong few-shot adaptation. Our code, pretraining data, and models are available on the project page to help the community reproduce our results.
summary_zh: 世界-动作模型联合预测未来的观测与动作，然而，面向重建的视觉表示并未明确强调操作所需的物体空间关系与状态变化。我们提出Phoenix，用于学习场景结构表示以支持世界-动作建模。具体而言，Phoenix编码器通过几何与时空语义知识的双教师蒸馏，丰富DINOv3的通用视觉语义。随后，CS-VAE以因果方式聚合并压缩Phoenix编码器特征为生成式潜变量，同时保留场景信息与空间布局。最后，Phoenix联合预测这些潜变量、互补的外观潜变量以及机器人动作，将场景演化与动作生成联系起来。为研究预训练数据效率，我们整理了约39,000小时的以自我为中心及机器人操作数据用于表示学习，并使用机器人演示子集进行世界-动作模型预训练。在遵循基准特定的后训练流程后，Phoenix在涵盖单臂、双臂及灵巧操作的仿真与真实机器人基准上均取得了最先进性能。其对扰动表现出强大的鲁棒性，在LIBERO-Plus上成功率达94.8%，在RoboTwin 2.0 C2R上达72.4%，同时在Bench2Dex和RoboDojo-RealWorld上分别展现出强跨具身迁移能力与真实世界操作性能。预训练规模分析表明，与仅使用视频VAE的基线相比，数据扩展带来了更大的性能提升，体现出更强的扩展收益与更高效的数据利用。此外，Phoenix在仅使用有限下游演示进行适配时仍保持高成功率，展现了强大的少样本适应能力。我们的代码、预训练数据及模型已在项目页面上公开，以帮助社区复现我们的结果。
tldr: Phoenix introduces a scene-structure representation learning method for world-action models, using dual-teacher distillation and a causal variational autoencoder to improve manipulation policy performance, robustness, and cross-embodiment transfer.
tldr_zh: Phoenix 提出了一种用于世界-动作模型的场景结构表示学习方法，通过双教师蒸馏和因果变分自编码器提升操作策略的性能、鲁棒性和跨具身迁移能力。

title: Grana: Compositional Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
summary: Robot reward modeling faces two challenges: generalizing across tasks and accurately tracking progress in long-horizon manipulation. General-purpose reward models demonstrate broad task transfer, but transfer from short-task pretraining to long-horizon tasks remains underexplored. Long-horizon progress models often rely on task-specific subtask classifiers or fixed action vocabularies, limiting the reuse of learned progress knowledge when adapting to new tasks. To address these challenges, we introduce Grana, a vision-language robot reward model that learns to identify unfinished subtasks and estimate their continuous progress using open-vocabulary subtask descriptions. We train a language-conditioned model to estimate progress in short-horizon tasks and individual subtasks of long-horizon tasks. For long-horizon tasks, we combine the selected subtask's predicted progress with credit for preceding completed subtasks to estimate whole-task progress. General progress prediction requires training the model across diverse tasks with progress supervision that accounts for imperfect execution. Elapsed-time proxies can misrepresent progress when relative subtask durations vary, or failures reverse local progress. We therefore introduce an annotation protocol that converts sparse subtask boundaries and action-quality annotations into dense progress targets, without requiring annotators to assign numerical progress scores. Pretraining with this supervision on 200 diverse, mostly short-horizon manipulation tasks enables zero-shot reward prediction on unseen tasks and improves progress prediction after adaptation to multi-minute, long-horizon tasks. Experiments demonstrate (i) generalizable reward prediction, including adaptation to five long-horizon tasks, (ii) benefits from pretraining and composing subtask progress estimates, and (iii) improved downstream policy performance.
summary_zh: 机器人奖励建模面临两大挑战：跨任务泛化以及长程操作中进度状态的精确追踪。通用奖励模型展现出广泛的任务迁移能力，但从短任务预训练到长程任务的迁移尚未得到充分探索。长程进度模型通常依赖特定任务的子任务分类器或固定动作词汇表，这限制了在适应新任务时对已学进度知识的复用。为应对上述挑战，我们提出Grana——一种视觉-语言机器人奖励模型，能够识别未完成的子任务，并利用开放词汇的子任务描述估计其连续进度。我们训练了一个语言条件模型，用于估计短程任务及长程任务中各子任务的进度。对于长程任务，我们将选中的子任务预测进度与已完成前序子任务的奖励相结合，以估计整体任务进度。通用进度预测要求模型在多样任务上进行训练，并采用能够反映不完美执行的进度监督。当相对子任务时长变化或失败导致局部进度回退时，基于已用时间的代理指标可能无法准确反映真实进度。为此，我们引入一种标注协议，将稀疏的子任务边界和动作质量标注转换为密集进度目标，而无需标注者为进度赋予数值评分。利用该监督信号在200个多样化、以短程为主的操控任务上进行预训练，使得模型能够对未见任务实现零样本奖励预测，并在适配分钟级长程任务后提升进度预测效果。实验结果表明：(i) 奖励预测具有良好泛化性，包括适配五个长程任务；(ii) 预训练及子任务进度估计的组合带来显著收益；(iii) 下游策略性能得以改善。
tldr: Grana is a vision-language reward model that uses open-vocabulary subtask descriptions to estimate continuous progress for long-horizon robot manipulation, trained with a novel annotation protocol and pretrained on diverse short-horizon tasks for zero-shot generalization.
tldr_zh: Grana 是一种视觉语言奖励模型，利用开放词汇的子任务描述来估计长时程机器人操作的连续进度，并通过新颖的标注协议和多样化的短时程任务预训练实现零样本泛化。

title: DiWALI: Diffusion Policy Learning in World Models via Latent Action Inference from Human and Robot Play
summary: Learning robot manipulation is constrained by the availability of action-labeled robot data, for both imitation and world models. Humans can demonstrate skills in seconds, but their demonstrations lack the required robot actions. We introduce DiWALI, a framework that learns and improves diffusion policies within a world model trained on human and robot play. DiWALI infers latent actions from consecutive frames using an inverse dynamics model, enabling world model training without action labels, and grounds them in robot commands through a decoder trained separately on robot play. Skill policies are trained over latent actions from action-free human demonstrations and improved with reinforcement learning in imagination. On the CALVIN benchmark, DiWALI policies trained solely from human demonstrations substantially outperform baselines trained with robot demonstrations. Incorporating human play into the world model training also yields stronger policies after fine-tuning than using the same amount of robot play alone. Experiments on a physical robot show that skills learned primarily from human demonstrations are further improved in imagination with a world model trained on human and robot play. Together, these results demonstrate that human experience can support both manipulation skill acquisition and subsequent policy improvement, reducing reliance on action-labeled robot data. Videos, dataset and code are available at https://diwali.cs.uni-freiburg.de.
summary_zh: 学习机器人操作受到动作标注机器人数据可用性的限制，这一点在模仿学习与世界模型中均有所体现。人类能够在数秒内展示技能，但其演示缺乏所需的机器人动作。我们提出了DiWALI，一个在基于人类与机器人互动数据训练的世界模型中学习并改进扩散策略的框架。DiWALI利用逆动力学模型从连续帧中推断潜在动作，使得无需动作标签即可训练世界模型，并通过单独在机器人互动数据上训练的解码器将这些潜在动作映射为机器人指令。技能策略基于无动作的人类演示中的潜在动作进行训练，并在想象环境中通过强化学习进行改进。在CALVIN基准测试上，仅依靠人类演示训练的DiWALI策略显著优于使用机器人演示训练的基线方法。将人类互动数据纳入世界模型训练后，微调得到的策略也优于单独使用相同数量的机器人互动数据。在实体机器人上的实验表明，主要从人类演示中习得的技能，能够在基于人类与机器人互动数据训练的世界模型中通过想象得到进一步提升。这些结果共同表明，人类经验既能支持操作技能的习得，也能促进后续的策略优化，从而减少对动作标注机器人数据的依赖。相关视频、数据集及代码可在 https://diwali.cs.uni-freiburg.de 获取。
tldr: DiWALI trains diffusion policies for robot manipulation inside a world model using latent actions inferred from human and robot play, reducing reliance on action-labeled robot data and enabling policy improvement via imagination on CALVIN and a real robot.
tldr_zh: DiWALI 在世界模型中利用从人类和机器人玩耍数据推断的潜在动作来训练扩散策略，减少对动作标签机器人数据的依赖，并在 CALVIN 和真实机器人上通过想象进行策略改进。

title: ActMem: From Latent Memory Reasoning to Grounded Robotic Action
summary:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in real-world long-horizon manipulation, where memory plays a crucial role.
  However, existing memory-augmented VLAs either retrieve past observations without reasoning about what they imply, or reason over the full
  history in a shared context where it crowds out current perception. Cognitive science treats them as distinct systems: memory reconstructs past
  experience to decide what to do, while perception guides how to act. We therefore propose ActMem, an in-context memory framework that
  decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding within a single vision-language backbone. Built on a vision-language model with native
  video understanding, ActMem infers the current subtask from a timestamped interaction history and keeps the hidden states formed during this
  inference as a Latent Memory Chain-of-Thought (Memory CoT), which conditions a flow-matching action expert. Perception Attention further lets
  the expert attend directly to the current view. To keep inference fast under long histories, Efficient Memory CoT Inference reuses computation
  across consecutive decisions without changing the output. ActMem achieves 71.1% task success and 80.8% completion success on RoboMemArena,
  surpassing the strongest baseline by 7.5 and 8.7 percentage points, and 73.8% average success on MIKASA-Robo, the best among all compared
  methods. In the real world, it reaches 68.8% average success on exogenous, endogenous, and traceless memory tasks, 10.0 percentage points above
  the strongest memory-augmented VLA. Code and checkpoints will be released at https://github.com/LigphiDonk/ActMem and
  https://huggingface.co/donk111/ActMem.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在真实世界长程操控任务中展现出令人鼓舞的性能，而记忆在此类任务中扮演着至关重要的角色。然而，现有的记忆增强型VLA模型要么仅检索过往观测而不对其含义进行推理，要么在共享上下文中对完整历史进行推理，从而挤占了当前感知的处理空间。认知科学将这两者视为不同的系统：记忆重构过往经验以决定做什么，而感知则引导如何行动。为此，我们提出ActMem——一种上下文记忆框架，在单一视觉-语言骨干网络内将记忆推理与感知锚定解耦。ActMem基于具备原生视频理解能力的视觉-语言模型，从带时间戳的交互历史中推断当前子任务，并将此推断过程中形成的隐状态保留为潜在记忆思维链（Memory CoT），用于条件化流匹配动作专家模块。感知注意力机制进一步使专家模块能够直接关注当前视角。为了在长历史条件下保持快速推理，高效记忆思维链推理（Efficient Memory CoT Inference）在连续决策间复用计算资源，且不改变输出结果。ActMem在RoboMemArena基准上达到71.1%的任务成功率和80.8%的完成成功率，分别超越最强基线7.5和8.7个百分点；在MIKASA-Robo基准上取得73.8%的平均成功率，在所有对比方法中表现最佳。在真实世界实验中，ActMem在外源性、内源性和无痕记忆任务上达到68.8%的平均成功率，比最强的记忆增强型VLA高出10.0个百分点。代码和模型权重将发布在 https://github.com/LigphiDonk/ActMem 和 https://huggingface.co/donk111/ActMem。
tldr: ActMem introduces an in-context memory framework for VLA models that decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding, using a latent Memory Chain-of-Thought to condition a flow-matching action expert. It achieves state-of-the-art success rates on RoboMemArena, MIKASA-Robo, and real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks.
tldr_zh: ActMem 提出了一种用于 VLA 模型的情境记忆框架，将记忆推理与感知接地解耦，利用潜在记忆思维链条件化流匹配动作专家。在 RoboMemArena、MIKASA-Robo 及真实世界长时程操作任务中取得了最先进的成功率。

title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
summary: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.
summary_zh: 具身智能旨在让机器人以类人的适应性和可靠性执行复杂的物理任务，这需要三种互补的能力：基于历史的认知推理、精准及时的物理执行，以及通过环境反馈实现推理与执行的组合。然而，现有基准要么在同一任务中同时评估推理与执行，要么分别评估两者而不考察其组合，因此难以揭示失败究竟源于推理、执行，还是二者的组合。我们提出了Mind2Act World，一个包含来自五个真实应用领域的30个模拟操作任务的诊断基准。每个任务设有三个难度级别和两种场景设置（干净场景和随机场景），共形成180种配置。这些任务构成三个视图：Mind测试基于历史观测的决策能力，Act测试精准及时的执行能力，而Mind2Act则在闭环任务中将两者结合，使动作结果指导后续决策。通过对比三个视图，可以判断系统是缺乏某种能力，还是无法组合其已具备的能力。诊断框架进一步将三个代表性系统的失败片段归因于Mind、Act或二者的组合，并以画像卡形式总结每个系统的表现。我们对多模态智能体、视觉-语言-动作模型（VLAs）和世界-动作模型（WAMs）的评估表明，单一视图中的能力并不能迁移到Mind2Act任务中。即使是最强的智能体，在Mind任务中成功率达52.7%，在Act任务中达39.0%，但在Mind2Act任务中仅有12.0%的成功率。最强智能体能够保持任务状态，但在持续接触方面存在困难，而端到端策略能执行已习得的动作，却难以保留任务状态。这些发现表明，通过环境反馈将推理与执行组合起来是当前面临的主要开放性难题。
tldr: Mind2Act World is a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated robotic manipulation tasks that separately and jointly evaluate history-based reasoning (Mind), physical execution (Act), and their composition (Mind2Act), revealing that state-of-the-art VLA and world-action models succeed individually but fail when composing reasoning and execution closed-loop.
tldr_zh: Mind2Act World 是一个包含30个模拟机器人操作任务的诊断基准，分别及联合评估基于历史的推理（Mind）、物理执行（Act）及其组合（Mind2Act），揭示最先进的VLA和世界动作模型在单独任务上表现良好，但在闭环组合推理与执行时失败。

title: Beyond the Sink Interpretation: Radial Attention in Flow-Based VLA Policies
summary: Prior work calls the high attention on the first and last action tokens of a flow-based VLA policy a radial action sink, and uses these tokens to set the execution horizon. In language models, a sink is a token with high incoming attention, a small value, and little effect on the output. We test whether that profile holds, not the horizon rule, in one $π_{0.5}$ checkpoint on five RoboCasa tasks. The two endpoints receive 5.4% of action-key mass, 1.4 percentage points above their uniform share, and rotary positional encoding produces this excess: directly in shallow layers and through upstream action-token RoPE deeper in the network. The endpoints do not fit the sink profile. Their value norms stay near the action-token mean in all 18 layers. On 250 paired episodes, masking them or zeroing their values changes success by less than 4 points, and replacing their value directions with those of another observation lowers it by 3.2 to 7.2 points across three donors, whereas the same replacement on two non-endpoint tokens in the executed prefix lowers it by 28.4 points. The token that does fit the sink profile on mass and value norm is the prefix BOS; on this checkpoint, zeroing its value raises success in two paired runs, by +13.2 points (95% CI [+7.0, +19.4]) and +6.0 points ([+0.2, +11.8]). Inside the action chunk, a relative-offset routing profile estimated on other tasks keeps 75% of action-token spread and keeps closed-loop success on three held-out tasks (42.7% against a 38.7% baseline), while uniform or shuffled routing drops success to 3-4%. High attention mass alone does not tell what a token does.
summary_zh: 先前研究将基于流式视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略中动作序列首尾两个动作标记所获得的高注意力关注称为“径向动作汇聚”（radial action sink），并利用这些标记设定执行时域。在语言模型中，“汇聚”（sink）指具有高入向注意力、数值较小且对输出影响甚微的标记。我们检验的是该特征描述是否成立，而非时域规则，具体在五个RoboCasa任务上对一个$π_{0.5}$检查点进行了测试。两个端点标记获得了5.4%的动作键（action-key）注意力质量，比其均匀份额高出1.4个百分点，而旋转位置编码（RoPE）正是产生这一超额注意力的原因：在浅层直接产生作用，并在网络深层通过上游动作标记的RoPE间接影响。端点标记不符合汇聚特征：在全部18层中，其值范数均保持在动作标记均值附近。在250对回合中，掩蔽或置零这些端点的值对成功率的影响不超过4个百分点；而用其他观察值的方向替换其值方向，在三个供体上使成功率降低3.2至7.2个百分点，相比之下，对执行前缀中两个非端点标记进行同样的替换则使成功率降低28.4个百分点。在质量和值范数上符合汇聚特征的是前缀BOS标记；在该检查点上，置零其值在两个配对运行中分别使成功率提高+13.2个百分点（95%置信区间[+7.0， +19.4]）和+6.0个百分点（[+0.2， +11.8]）。在动作块内部，基于其他任务估计的相对偏移路由配置保留了75%的动作标记扩展度，并在三个保留任务上保持了闭环成功率（42.7%，对比基线38.7%），而均匀或随机路由则使成功率骤降至3-4%。仅凭高注意力质量并不能揭示标记的实际功能。
tldr: This paper investigates whether the high attention on endpoint action tokens in a flow-based VLA policy constitutes a 'radial action sink' and finds it does not; instead, the prefix BOS token fits the sink profile, and routing action tokens by relative offsets preserves performance, suggesting attention mass alone is not indicative of token function.
tldr_zh: 本文研究基于流的VLA策略中端点动作token的高注意力是否构成'径向动作汇'，发现并非如此；相反，前缀BOS token符合汇特征，且按相对偏移路由动作token可保持性能，表明注意力权重本身不能反映token功能。

title: Alignment Drives Reuse: Learning Generalizable Robot-Use Agents from Heterogeneous Experience
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate broad generalization across tasks and domains. However, comparable generalization in robot manipulation remains challenging. Heterogeneity in robot embodiments, task formulations, geometric conventions, and action interfaces fragments interaction experience across benchmarks and hardware. We rethink robot skill learning through alignment: Can heterogeneous interactions across benchmarks and embodiments jointly improve one shared skillset for robot manipulation? We propose UniCraft, a framework for learning robot manipulation skills by aligning heterogeneous settings. Specifically, UniCraft represents observed scene geometry using consistent coordinate conventions and aligns sensing and control interfaces across robots. It organizes tasks from different benchmarks in a canonical format, allowing interaction feedback to jointly refine shared skills and the orchestration policy that guides their selection and composition, without any demonstrations or model weight updates. We interleave tasks from 3 benchmarks and 6 embodiments, collecting 2,700 learning rollouts per agent model. During training, UniCraft improves pooled task success on unseen scenarios and tasks by 9-28 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO, 10.8-13.3 on RoboTwin 2.0, and 3.1-14.4 on RoboCasa365 (Epochs 1-3). After training, with the learned skills frozen, UniCraft demonstrates zero-shot transfer across 4 new robot embodiments and 5 additional agent models on robosuite and RoboDojo.
summary_zh: 视觉-语言模型（VLMs）在跨任务和跨领域展示了广泛的泛化能力。然而，在机器人操作中实现同等程度的泛化仍然具有挑战性。机器人本体、任务表述、几何约定及动作接口的异构性，使得跨基准测试和硬件平台上的交互经验呈现碎片化状态。我们通过对齐（alignment）重新思考机器人技能学习：异构的跨基准和跨本体交互能否共同提升一套共享的机器人操作技能？我们提出UniCraft，一个通过对齐异构设置来学习机器人操作技能的框架。具体而言，UniCraft采用一致的坐标约定来表示观测到的场景几何，并对齐不同机器人的感知与控制接口。它将来自不同基准测试的任务组织为规范格式，使得交互反馈能够共同优化共享技能以及引导技能选择与组合的编排策略，而无需任何示范数据或模型权重更新。我们将来自3个基准测试和6种机器人本体的任务交错进行，每种代理模型收集2,700次学习交互。训练过程中，UniCraft在未见场景和任务上的汇总任务成功率分别提升了：LIBERO-PRO上9–28个百分点，RoboTwin 2.0上10.8–13.3个百分点，RoboCasa365（第1–3轮）上3.1–14.4个百分点。训练完成后，在保持所学技能冻结的条件下，UniCraft展示了在robosuite和RoboDojo上的零样本迁移能力，覆盖4种新机器人本体和5种额外的代理模型。
tldr: UniCraft aligns heterogeneous robot interaction data across embodiments and benchmarks to jointly improve a shared manipulation skillset and orchestration policy, demonstrating zero-shot transfer to new embodiments without demonstrations or weight updates.
tldr_zh: UniCraft 通过对齐不同机器人和基准的异构交互数据，联合改进共享操作技能和编排策略，无需演示或权重更新即可零样本迁移到新本体。

title: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
summary: Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both. To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor. These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment. On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate. Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.
summary_zh: 大型多模态模型能够支持长时程机器人操作，但频繁调用模型会带来显著的延迟和令牌成本。核心挑战在于判断何时需要智能体辅助或干预，以及错误是否需要修正机器人执行、子任务规划，或两者兼而有之。为解决这一问题，我们提出了RoC（按需推理）框架，一种高效框架，通过在线任务状态监控器协调低层策略与高层推理智能体。该监控器将时序视觉观测与有序交互记忆相结合，共同估计当前子任务内的进展并预测其后续子任务。这些预测引导事件触发的智能体审查，以实现协同的执行修复与规划修订。验证结果用于管理记忆更新与子任务转换，使得常规执行由策略负责，而推理则聚焦于需要额外评估的决策。在RMBench上，RoC相比最强的基于智能体的基线，任务成功率提升了24.0个百分点，同时令牌消耗减少了65.3%。在任务成功率方面，它也优于最强的基于策略的基线，高出15.1个百分点。真实世界实验进一步验证了其在三项长时程操作任务中的有效性。总体而言，RoC支持高效智能体干预以及跨执行与规划维度的协同恢复，适用于长时程机器人操作。
tldr: RoC is an efficient agentic framework for long-horizon robot manipulation that uses a task-state monitor to trigger high-level reasoning only when needed, improving success and reducing token use.
tldr_zh: RoC 是一种用于长时程机器人操作的高效智能体框架，通过任务状态监控器按需触发高级推理，在提升成功率的同时大幅降低令牌消耗。

title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
summary: Off-road vision-language-action (VLA) models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference. Reusing a prediction reduces this demand while leaving its commands exposed to changes in vehicle motion. FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution. Its training-free interface maintains decoded plans between visual predictions. A speed-curvature action buffer is aligned with measured motion at each update, integrated into a local trajectory, and advanced by consuming the current action. The corrected remainder is written back to the buffer, preserving motion corrections across successive updates. A bounded refresh rule normalizes speed and curvature variations within a newly decoded plan and assigns a short or long reuse budget according to the resulting plan-roughness score. The interface requires neither backbone features nor an additional learned driving policy. Over a 3 s horizon, independent real-request evaluation achieves average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) of 0.328/0.596 m on ORAD-3D and 0.266/0.526 m on RELLIS-3D, reducing FDE by 18.0% and 36.7% at request rates of 6.0% and 4.8%, respectively. These runs retain lower errors across four backbones and both datasets and reduce Qwen3-VL request-processing cost by factors of 16.6 and 20.8 under serial replay, while mechanism and motion-only controls identify persistent state correction as the main source of the observed accuracy benefit. The source code and evaluation materials are publicly available at https://github.com/ADEPT-ORG/FastRoverVLA.
summary_zh: 越野视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型能够生成基于场景条件的规划轨迹，但频繁的轨迹更新会反复触发昂贵的多模态推理调用。复用预测结果可降低这一计算需求，但复用后的指令可能无法适应车辆运动状态的变化。FastRoverVLA通过将视觉规划生成与运动条件执行解耦，解决了这一不匹配问题。其免训练接口在视觉预测之间保持已解码的规划轨迹。在每个更新周期，一个速度-曲率动作缓冲区与实测运动状态对齐，集成至局部轨迹中，并通过消耗当前动作向前推进。修正后的剩余轨迹被写回缓冲区，从而在连续更新之间保留运动修正信息。一个有界的刷新规则对最新解码规划中的速度与曲率变化进行归一化处理，并根据计算得到的规划粗糙度评分分配短或长的复用预算。该接口既不需要骨干网络特征，也不依赖额外学习的驾驶策略。在3秒预测时域内，独立真实请求评估在ORAD-3D数据集上实现了平均位移误差（ADE）和最终位移误差（FDE）分别为0.328/0.596米，在RELLIS-3D数据集上分别为0.266/0.526米，在请求率分别为6.0%和4.8%时，FDE分别降低了18.0%和36.7%。这些运行在四种骨干网络和两个数据集上均保持了更低的误差，并在串行复用模式下将Qwen3-VL请求处理成本分别降低了16.6倍和20.8倍。机制消融与仅运动控制实验表明，持续状态修正观测到的精度提升的主要来源。源代码和评估材料已在 https://github.com/ADEPT-ORG/FastRoverVLA 公开提供。
